title.rendered: City of Tshwane Health Department to host diabetes outreach in Mamelodi

content.rendered:
On 13 September 2024, the City of Tshwane Health Department will host the first of two diabetes outreach programmes for 2024. This first outreach programme will take place at Mamelodi West Community Hall.

Diabetes is considered as a chronic disease of public health concern. According to the national Department of Health, the three common categories of diabetes include Type 1, where the blood glucose (sugar) level is too high as the body produces very little or no insulin; Type 2, which is due to lifestyle factors such as obesity, lack of physical activity or hereditary factors; and Type 3, which is gestational diabetes mellitus. This temporary condition develops in women, mostly during pregnancy, and has the potential to cause health problems in both mother and baby. Untreated diabetes can lead to stroke, nerve damage, blindness, kidney failure, heart attack and amputations.

Given the seriousness of this disease, interested community members are encouraged to attend the outreach programme and learn about the available services on diabetes and the aspects of care for diabetic people as well as the comprehensive package of other health promotion services. In partnership with various stakeholders, the following services will be available on the day: Blood pressure and blood glucose screening, eyecare and footcare, oral health screening, tuberculosis and HIV screening, drug and substance use awareness, gender-based violence awareness, mental health awareness, occupational health, physiotherapy and nutrition information.

As a demonstration of our commitment to bring services closer to communities, we will be partnering with the following stakeholders and sponsors: The Gauteng Department of Health, Wits Reproductive Health and HIV Institute (Wits RHI), the Aurum Institute, the Moses Mabhida Foundation, Sungardens Palliative Care, Voice It In Action, Thandanani Drop Inn Centre, Phokwane Funeral Directors and Synexus.

These outreach programmes aim to highlight the importance of regular screening and testing related to health matters. Early detection can save lives.

The second diabetes outreach programme is planned for 25 October2024 at Hercules Clinic.

On Wednesday, 28 August 2024, the City of Tshwane will carry out an upgrade and tie-in connection to the water supply network in Raslouw Ext 16, on the corner of Jewel Beetle Street and Lochner Road.

This essential work is scheduled for ten hours, from 08:00 to 18:00, and it may result in a water supply interruption in the following areas:

  • Raslouw Ext 19 and 20
  • Portion 129, Swartkop 383-JR

The City of Tshwane apologises for the inconvenience that may be caused due to the above-mentioned work.

Residents are urged to continue to make the following water-conservation measures part of their normal lifestyle:

  • Do not water or irrigate gardens with hosepipes or sprinkler systems between 06:00 and 18:00.
  • Do not wash vehicles with hosepipes.
  • Do not fill swimming pools.
  • Install a low-flow shower head and tap aerators, where possible.
  • Use a dual-flush toilet cistern.
  • Plant indigenous or drought-resistant shrubs in the garden.
  • Use a broom instead of a hosepipe when cleaning driveways or patios.
  • Collect rainwater to reuse in the garden or wash the car.
  • Cover the swimming pool to reduce water evaporation.
  • Take a short shower rather than a bath.
  • Close a running tap while brushing teeth or shaving.
  • Regularly check toilets and taps for leaks.

Residents are urged to continue using grey water to water gardens and flush toilets. Where possible, water-saving devices should be installed.

Residents are further urged to report water leaks, burst pipes and all incidents where water is wasted on the following numbers:

 

Incident Telephone number
No water supply, burst water pipes, leaking meters or blocked street sewers 012 358 9999 or 080 1111 556
Illegal water connections 012 358 9060
Non-payment 012 345 8514
Account enquiries 012 358 9999

title.rendered: City of Tshwane on track to provide clean water in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                             20 August 2024

Ald Cilliers Brink

Executive Mayor of Tshwane

 

The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce significant progress in our ongoing efforts to deliver clean, potable water to the residents of Hammanskraal. During a recent community imbizo held on 17 August 2024 at Makgoba Sebothoma Hall in Hammanskraal, key updates were provided on the advancement of critical water infrastructure projects, including the Phase 1 upgrading of Klipdrift Water Treatment Plant and the Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant.

The engagement provided a platform for residents to engage directly with the panel during a question-and-answer session, fostering an open dialogue about the project’s impact and progress.

The City remains vigilant in overseeing both Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant and Klipdrift Water Treatment Plant projects. We are committed to addressing any potential delays and acts of sabotage and ensuring the appointment of credible contractors. We will continue to update residents on project progress and work towards eliminating the need for water tankers by ensuring clean, potable drinking water for all. Moving away from water tankers will enable us to repurpose aging infrastructure and advance service delivery.

We value the trust of our community and will continue to build and reaffirm this trust through transparent communication and dedicated efforts. As part of our efforts, we have completed a thorough audit of water meters across 37 620 households. Of these, 23 616 meters were found to be in good working order, while 14 004 meters are scheduled for replacement between September and November 2024.

Recognising the financial burden on our residents, we will be presenting some resolutions to Council on writing off historical debt associated with the audited meters. This decision will provide residents a fresh start with new potable tap water available in their homes, eliminating the reliance on water tankers.

I want to acknowledge the Deputy Mayor, Cllr Nasiphi Moya, and the MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination, Cllr Themba Fosi, who have been conducting monthly oversight visits to keep regular watch on the projects and have been instrumental in ensuring that the City remains on track with our work to provide water to Hammanskraal residents.

I also want to thank the Speaker of Council, Cllr Mncedi Ndzwanana, for organising the community imbizo.

Our interventions in Hammanskraal represent the most significant progress made by any administration in the past 20 years.

Media enquiries:

Sipho Stuurman

(siphost@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: City of Tshwane makes significant progress on provision of clean drinking water in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                             14 August 2024

Cllr Themba Fosi

MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination

 

The City of Tshwane would like to provide a progress update on two critical projects aimed at improving water supply to our residents in Hammanskraal, namely Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant and Magalies Water Package Plant that is meant to provide tap water as an interim measure while Rooiwal upgrades are underway.

Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant progress

The Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant upgrade is a key project in the City’s commitment to providing clean potable water to our residents. Construction has officially commenced, marking a significant step towards the City’s efforts to enhance the plant’s waste water treatment capacity.

To date, substantial progress has been made across various components of the project. The installation of the Clear Vu fence at both the north and east works is nearly complete, with 93% and 100% installed, respectively. Key mechanical and electrical repairs are underway, including the completion of blowers and belt press installations.

 Over the next three months, we anticipate advancing the construction of two primary sedimentation tanks, the refurbishment of the east flow balancing tank and pump station, and the upgrading of the anaerobic digesters at Rooiwal West Works.

Our teams are also focused on accelerating milestones to ensure timely completion, with additional resources being mobilised to fast-track cleaning and repairs.

The City is working in partnership with the Department of Water and Sanitation, the National Treasury and the Development Bank of Southern Africa, as the managing agent, in a collaborative effort to accelerate solutions to Hammanskraal’s water challenges.

Magalies Water Package Plant

While construction work is underway at Rooiwal, the City recognises that residents want water from their taps and not from water tankers. Therefore, as an interim measure, the City has partnered with Magalies Water and the Department of Water and Sanitation to deliver potable tap water to affected Hammanskraal areas.

As part of this intervention, the City has audited 37 620 households, with 23 616 water meters confirmed to be in good working condition. However, about 14 004 meters will be replaced between September and November 2024. This is a critical step in preparing for the supply of clean potable water from Magalies Water Package Plant to Hammanskraal residents, starting in September 2024.

The City has also taken a decision to write off historic debt associated with the audited meters, giving residents an opportunity to start afresh with new potable tap water available in their homes.

Community imbizo

To further engage with our residents and provide detailed updates, we will hold an imbizo on 17 August 2024. The Executive Mayor, Ald Cilliers Brink, the Deputy Mayor, Cllr Nasiphi Moya, Speaker of Council, Cllr Mncedi Ndzwanana along with myself as the MMC tasked with leading the department responsible for water services, will lead the City’s delegation and engage the community on the progress we are making.

The imbizo will provide information on the expected arrival date of clean water in Hammanskraal, starting in September 2024. We invite residents from the three affected wards to join us for this important engagement.

We remain committed to ensuring access to clean water for all residents and we are pleased by the progress made under this administration. Our interventions in Hammanskraal represent the most significant progress made by any administration in the past 20 years.

 Enquiries:

Tsebo Majoro

tseboma@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: Update on water outage in Tshwane following Rand Water’s infrastructure maintenance of its systems that supply bulk water to Gauteng metros

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce that there has been a gradual improvement in the City’s bulk and distribution systems which are fed by Rand Water’s Mapleton System.

The City’s system ran dry following Rand Water’s infrastructure maintenance work on its Mapleton System, which took 77 hours (three days and five hours) to be completed. This exercise started on Friday, 26 July 2024, and ended on Monday morning. During that period, there was no pumping to the Mapleton System. This left various areas in Regions 2, 3 and 6 without water, compelling the City to dispatch water tankers to the affected areas.

It is important to note that the City of Tshwane, like other metros in Gauteng, receives 79% of its bulk water supply from Rand Water’s two booster pumping stations, Mapleton and Palmiet. Rand Water has to first replenish its own reservoirs fed from the Mapleton and Palmiet Systems before it can begin to distribute water to its municipal customers.

This process can take up to two weeks for the network to fully recover. This, however, does not imply that the water supply will be restored in two weeks’ time.

It is encouraging to note that, even though the gradual build-up of the water supply is at a slow pace, some residents in the areas that were without water have confirmed water flowing from their taps.

The following areas have started to receive water:

  • Die Wilgers
  • Eersterust
  • Silverton
  • Waltloo
  • Wapadrand

The areas that are still without water will continue to be serviced by water tankers. The deployment of water trucks is being coordinated through the relevant ward councillors.

 The City is pleading once more with residents in the low-lying areas to use water sparingly when the supply is restored to allow our bulk water system and reservoirs to recover quickly.

The City apologises for the inconvenience caused by this planned water supply interruption.

title.rendered: Update on Rand Water’s infrastructure maintenance of its systems that supply water to the City of Tshwane

content.rendered:
Rand Water has notified the City of Tshwane that the infrastructure maintenance work on its Mapleton System has been completed. The water utility’s team of technicians managed to timeously complete the work, which started on Friday, 26 July 2024, and ended this morning. The maintenance period took 77 hours (three days and five hours) without any pumping.

During the maintenance period, various areas in Regions 2, 3 and 6 experienced water supply interruptions, compelling the City to dispatch water tankers to the affected areas. Currently, the City’s entire bulk and distribution systems that are fed by the Mapleton System are empty.

It is encouraging to note that Rand Water’s team is currently charging the pipelines. Once charging has been completed, pumping to the Mapleton System will resume. Residents are urged to exercise patience during the pumping period as the network takes two weeks to fully recover before it reaches the required pressure. The City will continue to provide water to its affected customers through roaming water tankers.

Rand Water is undertaking its final maintenance on the Palmiet System for 40 hours today from 05:00 until Tuesday, 30 July 2024, at 21:00. Pumping will be reduced to 76% during this period.

The City is pleading once more with residents in the low-lying areas to use water sparingly when the supply is restored to allow our bulk water system and reservoirs to recover quickly.

The City apologises for the inconvenience caused by this planned water supply interruption.

title.rendered: Update: Water supply interruption affecting Zithobeni and nearby areas

content.rendered:
This morning, a team of technicians from the City of Tshwane Bulk Water Supply Section commenced with the installation of a new pipe to replace the burst pipe that supplies Zithobeni Reservoir in Region 7.

The new pipe was delivered at the workshop for fabrication yesterday prior to installation. Subsequent to the installation of the new pipe, the team will proceed to the second part of the repair work, which is the connection of the y-pipe. If all goes well, it is estimated that all the work should be completed by this evening.

The City would like to alert customers that after the successful installation of the new pipe, technicians still have to test pumping, and because the reservoir and the network are empty, the pipeline will have to fill up first before the reservoir can start building up pressure.

The water supply will be restored gradually to the low-lying areas first before the high-lying areas can experience water flow from their taps.

It is unfortunate that our customers in Zithobeni had to endure a prolonged water outage following complications which developed when the City’s technicians were fixing a major leak on a main bulk pipeline that supplies Zithobeni Reservoir last week on Wednesday, 12 June 2024. These delays were not anticipated, however, the technical team is working around the clock to ensure that the water supply to the area is restored as soon as possible.

The City understands your frustrations and appreciates your patience during this very difficult period.

The City will retain the roaming water tankers in the affected areas until the water supply is fully restored. As and when the situation dictates, the City will consider increasing the number of tankers to meet the demand.

 Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane cancels water tanker tender before it is awarded

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                 18 June 2024

Cllr Jacqui Uys

MMC for Finance

Earlier this year, the City of Tshwane advertised a tender to appoint a panel for the supply of water tankers as rudimentary services in informal areas. The City has now taken decisive action to cancel this tender before the award to prevent any possible corruption.

This comes as a result of newly implemented corruption-detection mechanisms in supply chain processes, which flagged that there was a leak of valuation documentation and a possible compromise in the tender specifications.

The tender specifications will now be reworked and the tender re-advertised. This decision reflects the City’s unwavering commitment to upholding the highest standards of accountability, integrity and fairness in operations.

While this will not impact the current supply of water tankers, it does highlight the harsh reality that water, even as a basic human right, is used by some to enrich themselves.

The City’s political leadership is committed to stopping the exploitation of vulnerable and poor residents. In this regard, we have also made the decision to spend 30% of the funds allocated to water tanker provision in the 2024/25 financial year to explore sustainable, long-term solutions for the supply of water to informal areas.

 

 Media enquiries

MMC Jacqui Uys

jacquiu@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: Rand Water to embark on extensive maintenance of its infrastructure that supplies water to Tshwane

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has been notified by Rand Water about its plan to embark on extensive maintenance of its infrastructure across Gauteng’s municipalities from 22 June to 29 July 2024.

The planned maintenance, according to the water utility, is aimed at preserving the lifespan of its infrastructure and improving its reliability during the higher summer demand period. This essential maintenance work will involve the replacement of Rand Water’s bulk water meters that supply various reservoirs in Tshwane.

Where possible, the affected reservoirs will be filled to maximum capacity prior to the maintenance work. However, the water supply may be interrupted during the upkeep period and residents are therefore urged to use water sparingly.

The City’s reservoirs that are supplied by Rand Water’s Palmiet System will be affected on different dates as follows.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane marks significant progress at Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant

content.rendered:
On Friday, 7 June 2024, the City of Tshwane Rooiwal Subcommittee visited Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant.

Along with my colleagues, Ald Hannes Coetzee and Cllr Themba Fosi, we were encouraged by the steady progress made by officials to ensure that Phase 1 of the refurbishment of Rooiwal is completed by April 2025.

The visit offered incredible insights into the tremendous progress being made in comparison to a previous visit conducted on 9 May 2024. There has been progress in securing the site with security personnel, with the future aim of installing camera surveillance. Other areas of improvement include equipment management and reinstallation, which have all been dealt with according to plan.

Other areas on track with the project plan include the completion of pumping sewage effluent and desludging. This means that the removal of scrapper down pipes and refurbishments will start this month.

When we handed the project over to the Development Bank of Southern Africa, we envisioned March 2025 as the deadline for general building and mechanical engineering and April 2025 for the Phase 1 completion deadline.

The importance of completing the refurbishments at Rooiwal will ensure that we can improve the quality of water that is discharged from the plant. Once the system runs steadily at the plant, we should be able to monitor the safety and quality of the water provided and its chemical distributions.

Our visit to Rooiwal also finalised the final steps to ensuring that Hammanskraal residents have access to clean water by September 2024. This deadline is still within our reach with the completion of the water meter readings project. Over 30 000 household meters were assessed during the programme.

We thank the residents of Hammanskraal for their cooperation and enabling us to complete our water meter audits two months ahead of schedule. We remain committed to exercising our political leadership to ensure the success of this project. The subcommittee will return to the area at the end of June 2024 for further oversight.

Enquiries:        Zintle Mahlati (zintlema@tshwane.gov.za)

Tsebo Majoro (tseboma@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: City of Tshwane and the Department of Water and Sanitation sign a Memorandum of Understanding to address the City’s water constraints

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has set the wheels in motion towards formalising strategic partnerships that will contribute towards addressing the City’s water and sanitation-related challenges.

The national Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS) is one of these strategic partners which the City has approached, not only to be involved as a regulator, but also to collaborate on issues such as leveraging DWS technical and financial resources to jointly address the City’s other challenges, such as the pollution of the Hennops River, upgrading Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works and inadequate human resources.

Today, 10 June 2024, the two parties signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on various strategic areas, such as infrastructure planning and development, water resource planning and infrastructure solutions, and capacity-building of City of Tshwane officials. Discussions are at an advanced stage to finalise a flagship engineering candidacy development programme, which will see the secondment of candidate engineers to the City and professional engineers who will be contracted to the City for a three-year period. This team of engineers has undergone training under the DWS.

In addition, the DWS will offer free mentorship through its database of mentors to the candidate engineers to assist them to obtain their professional registration with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA). Once implemented successfully, the programme will assist the City to comply with the new ECSA Identification of Engineering Work Regulations.

The MoU was signed by the City Manager of the City of Tshwane, Mr Johann Mettler, and DWS Deputy Director-General for Water and Sanitation Services, Dr Risimati Mathye, at the City’s headquarters, Tshwane House.

During the signing ceremony, Mettler said: “Addressing our major water challenges requires a collaborative effort between the City and key water stakeholders, and the DWS is one of those key players. We have been facing significant water challenges which have negatively affected some of our residents for a longer period. Some of these challenges can be linked to ageing infrastructure and maintenance challenges at some of our water treatment plants.”

Dr Mathye said that the collaboration between the two entities is a significant one, particularly on the DWS side, to fulfil its role as a regulator of the water and sanitation sector.

“We are pleased by the will and zeal that has been shown by the City in ensuring collaborative efforts and allowing us to work together in different spheres of government to ensure efficient services to the residents of Tshwane. It has always been our intention to work with all municipalities at local government level to capacitate them where we can to achieve Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 6, to realise clean water and decent sanitation provision to communities,” Dr Mathye emphasized.

The other key areas of collaboration that the MoU will focus on include the following:

  • Water resource planning and infrastructure solutions in line with the City’s Climate Action Plan
  • Infrastructure planning and development
  • Collaboration on water and sanitation-related programmes
  • Sustainable Development Goal 6: Clean water and sanitation
  • Training and capacity-building, including secondment of staff between the parties
  • Education and awareness campaigns (such as National Water Week)
  • Knowledge-sharing (jointly hosting seminars and conferences)
  • Benchmarking programmes, such as Green Drop, Blue Drop and No Drop
  • Joint enforcement programmes to prevent water pollution
  • Exploration of alternative water and sanitation technologies with DWS and its entities
  • Key bulk infrastructure in line with the Metropolitan Spatial Development Framework and Regional Spatial Development Frameworks
  • Any other additional area that the parties may agree to collaborate on in future

The signed MoU reinforces the ideal of the Intergovernmental Relations Act, 2005 (Act 13 of 2005), which implores a concerted effort by government in all spheres to work together and to integrate, as far as possible, their actions in the provision of services, the alleviation of poverty and the development of society.

title.rendered: City makes progress towards the provision of clean water to Hammanskraal residents

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                  13 May 2024

Cllr Nasiphi Moya

Deputy Mayor

In my capacity as Deputy Mayor, along with the MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination, Cllr Themba Fosi, and the MMC for Region 2, Ald Hannes Coetzee, we conducted an oversight visit to the Rooiwal Infrastructure Upgrade Project on Friday.

Significant progress has been made, with both the general building and mechanical and electrical contractors on-site and actively working on an accelerated plan to enhance the efficiency and functionality of the plant.

One of the key milestones of this project is the assessment of the quality of the effluent discharged from the plant. Thanks to the proactive efforts of our contractors, we are optimistic that by December 2024 we will start having measurable data on the improved quality of the effluent being discharged.

In another crucial development, preparations are well underway to provide clean water to the residents of Hammanskraal by September 2024. We are proud to report that our audit team has successfully assessed over 23 000 households out of the initial target of 39 000. This puts us two months ahead of our scheduled timeline and demonstrates our commitment to delivering clean water to the community in a timely manner.

We remain dedicated to the successful completion of the Rooiwal Infrastructure Upgrade Project and pledge to continue working diligently towards achieving our goals. We appreciate the ongoing support of all stakeholders involved in this vital project.

Enquiries:

Gauta Komane

gautak@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: City of Tshwane conducts water meter audits in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                  16 April 2024

Cllr Nasiphi Moya

Deputy Mayor

Community and Social Development Services

The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce the commencement of a water meter audit drive in Hammanskraal this week. The initiative follows the recent launch of the Magalies Water Package Plant project, which aims to ensure clean water supply to the residents of Hammanskraal by September 2024.

The audit team has started their work in Hammanskraal West and is scheduled to cover all affected areas within Hammanskraal by 31 July 2024.

Following the auditing process, water meter replacements and new water meter installations will be concluded by 30 September 2024 as more meters might be identified for replacement during the audit.

As part of the meter audit process, City officials and contracted service providers will also do data collection in the area. This will involve activities such as opening and closing water taps, recording water meter numbers and readings, and confirming physical and street addresses.

The city calls on Hammanskraal residents to please cooperate with officials and service providers during the audit process. It is essential for residents to allow access to their yards for the necessary inspections. A successful audit will ensure that the City’s water systems are prepared to receive and supply water to the affected areas in Hammanskraal.

In my capacity as the Deputy Mayor together with MMC for Utility Services Cllr Themba Fosi, we will both play an oversight role over the meter auditing process in order ensure that we deliver metered drinking tap water for the people of Hammanskraal.

For confirmation of the auditors’ identities, residents can contact the City of Tshwane on 012 358 9062.

 Enquiries for Deputy Mayor: Dr Azwihangwisi Judith Mphidi

azwihangwisim@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: City of Tshwane condemns possible sabotage of water infrastructure in Rethabiseng

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane, in the strongest possible terms, condemns probable acts of sabotage by characters who are depriving residents of their right to clean, potable water in and around the Rethabiseng area, which is situated between Bronkhorstspruit and Ekangala in Region 7.

Yesterday, 19 March 2024, the City reported that water had been restored in Ekangala and Rethabiseng, with the exception of Rethabiseng Ext 4, due to challenges experienced with the infrastructure network connection.

Some parts of Region 7, particularly Rethabiseng and Ekangala, had experienced a prolonged water outage caused by the breakdown of a pump at Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant. As a mitigating factor, water tankers were dispatched to the affected areas during that period.

Shortly after water supply had been restored and deployment of the water tankers was stopped, reports emerged from some quarters in the affected areas which indicate possible sabotage in the form of tampering with the City’s infrastructure.

Today, the City received information that a Mahindra bakkie which was spotted in Rethabiseng Ext 4 is suspected to be involved in meddling with water valves in the area. It is presumed that the alleged saboteurs of the water infrastructure are the drivers of the bakkie in question. This supposition is yet to be proven.

Officials from the Tshwane Metro Police Department (TMPD) have been activated to conduct operations in the area.

Residents are urged to write down the registration numbers of questionable vehicles and to report them immediately to the TMPD on 012 358 7095/7096. This number is manned 24/7.

Meanwhile, there were allegations earlier today that tap water in Riamarpark was brownish in colour, sparking fears of possible impurity. The City moved swiftly to conduct sampling in the said area, and it was discovered that the water is colourless.

The City of Tshwane calls on the clique allegedly involved in the disruption of clean, drinkable water in the region to immediately desist from doing so, as this not only threatens service delivery, but also endangers the health of residents.

 Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane and Coca-Cola Beverages South Africa open a borehole in Gomora Informal Settlement

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                    19 March 2024

Cllr Ofentse Madzebatela

MMC for Human Settlements

 

On Monday 18 March 2024, I joined Coca-Cola Beverages South Africa (CCBSA) for the official opening of a borehole for the Malusi/Gomora Informal Settlement at the Malusi Youth Development Organisation Community Centre in Pretoria West.

The CCBSA approached the City’s Human Settlements Department with a proposal for a solar-powered groundwater-harvesting project to drill a borehole to partially address the water needs of the community.

Currently, the settlement receives rudimentary services through water tankers and chemical toilets in the absence of engineering services in the area. This is a result of the ongoing service delivery challenges in the area that continue to affect the provision of water to the community.

The opening of this borehole comes at a time where Gauteng is experiencing water-scarcity challenges. As a City, we welcome the innovative work by the CCBSA to address a social challenge in their community by maximising own water-generation capacity.

Equally important is that the location of the borehole forms part of the existing formalisation project located on the Remainder of Portion 21, 124, 150 and 227 of the farm Zandfontein 317-JR, also known as the proposed township Kirkney Ext 68, and will go a long way to provide safe drinking water to residents.

The City of Tshwane stands firm on our whole-of-society approach to better service delivery by working with businesses, communities and individuals to make a City that works for all its people.

We remain committed to address water challenges in informal areas and to provide clean and drinkable water to all residents of Tshwane.

title.rendered: Tshwane Ya Tima completes electricity and water disconnections worth about R70 million in one day

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                               13 March 2024

Cllr Cilliers Brink

Executive Mayor of Tshwane

On Tuesday, 12 March 2024, I led a Tshwane Ya Tima revenue-collection campaign that completed electricity disconnections worth R53,1 million and water restrictions and disconnections worth R13,2 million in various areas of the city.

This included two businesses in Pretoria West, which had tampered with their meters and owe the City a combined R6,3 million, R2,3 million in Elardus Park and R970 000 from a guesthouse.

We continue to observe many illegal connections from defaulting clients who run up high service bills and fail to pay the City. The Tshwane Ya Tima team will be monitoring these areas after the cut-off operations and ensure that those who illegally reconnect face the music.

Illegal connections are a criminal offence and the City will use Section 300 of the Criminal Procedure Act, 1977 (Act 51 of 1977) to go after offenders and claim compensation.

I would like to thank those who pay for their services. By honouring your obligation, you enable improved service delivery. Residents who are struggling to keep up with their payments are reminded to make payment arrangements at any of our customer care centres. Do not wait for the City to come and disconnect your services!

We need to stop the culture of non-payment as everyone must pay for what they consume. The City needs revenue to deliver services and to honour commitments to creditors such as Eskom and Rand Water.

We are firm in our stance that the financial rescue of the City is non-negotiable, therefore, every effort must be made to restore the City to a financially healthy position as quickly as possible.

title.rendered: Update: Installation of pump and motor at Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant expected to be completed this evening

content.rendered:
The installation of the pump and motor at Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant is currently progressing well and completion is expected this evening.

If the installation is successful, a few tests will be run, and if the outcome is positive, pumping will commence in earnest.

Once pumping has commenced, which is expected to take place either later tonight or earliest tomorrow morning, it will take a few days for the system to recover and stabilise before the full water supply is restored to all the areas in Region 7.

The City will continue balancing the system by switching the current supply between areas in order to ensure an equitable distribution of the water supply. Water tankers will also continue to be dispatched to the affected areas.

Plans are still firmly on track, glitches notwithstanding, to restore the water supply to the distraught residents of Region 7, as per the commitments and undertakings made by the City.

The City understands the frustration that these residents have endured for a prolonged period and appreciates their patience during this very difficult period.

The City is working on a long-term plan to not just repair the pumps in the event of a breakdown, but to entirely replace the current ones. To this end, two new pumps will be ordered for the plant, and additional capacity will be sourced for the technical skills required to improve the management of the plant.

The City is embarking on erecting a new fence around the plant to better secure the plant and prevent access, which we suspect is conducive to sabotage and arson. A contractor has already visited the site to conduct an assessment and will furnish the City with a quotation.

Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: Soshanguve MM water and sewer reticulation project well on track for completion

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                          20 February 2024

Cllr Ofentse Madzebatela

MMC for Human Settlements

Today, I conducted an oversight visit to Soshanguve MM in Region 1 where the Human Settlements Department is constructing water and sewer reticulation infrastructure.

The project, currently at 80% completion rate, is expected to be handed over to the community by the end of June 2024. At least 80 households will benefit from this infrastructure.

This water and sewer reticulation project is expected to contribute to the City’s strategic intent of moving away from providing our residents with rudimentary water and sanitation using mobile water tankers and rudimentary toilets, thereby providing our most valuable stakeholders with dignity.

The City has budgeted about R262 million for the provision of water through mobile tankers throughout Tshwane in the current financial year (2023/24). It is our intention as the multiparty government to incrementally reduce this in the medium to long term by investing in the construction of critical bulk water infrastructure.

Providing the residents of Tshwane with access to dignified water and sewer services remains a priority of the multiparty government.

title.rendered: Public participation on the notarial lease of the remainder of ERF 6957, Mamelodi and a portion of the remainder of the farm Mabopane 702-JR

content.rendered:
Media advisory                                                                                             15 February 2024

Office of the Speaker

In accordance with Regulations 5 and 35 of the Municipal Asset Transfer Regulations, read with Section 21A of the Local Government: Municipal Systems Act, 2000 (Act 32 of 2000), the Office of the Speaker hereby invites all interested stakeholders and community members to submit comments on the proposed lease of the Remainder of Erf 6957, Mamelodi (known as HM Pitje Stadium) and a Portion of the Remainder of the farm Mabopane 702-JR (known as Odi Stadium).

The dilapidated state of the HM Pitje and Odi Stadiums has also been the focal point at national government and provincial legislature levels, culminating in deliberations around the state of these stadiums at the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Sport, Arts and Culture. Interest has also been received from professional football clubs, specifically in relation to the rehabilitation of HM Pitje Stadium.

The proposal is meant to drive local economic growth, and this will serve as an incentive for local football franchises to invest in township stadiums with outright control on the running and operation of these stadiums. Other key benefits of this proposal to the City include the following:

  • Creating safer communities – Communities have constantly lamented the dangers associated with the current dilapidated facilities. Additionally, it is envisaged that the stadiums will be converted into multifunctional sporting precincts (particularly HM Pitje Stadium), and this will open up sporting and recreational opportunities for various communities.
  • Unlocking the full value of the two facilities to ensure their optimal use – This will also unlock other spill-over opportunities in economic activities such as township tourism and the broader township economy.

The City intends granting lease rights over the stadiums over a period of 80 years comprising an initial lease of 50 years with a once-off option to renew the lease for a further 30 years. Over the duration of the lease, the City will receive rental revenue.

Members of the media, residents and stakeholders are invited as follows:

Saturday, 24 February 2024 10:00 HM Pitje Stadium Mamelodi West Community Hall
Sunday, 25 February 2024 10:00 Odi Stadium Mabopane Indoor Sport Centre
Tuesday, 27 February 2024 18:00 HM Pitje Stadium and Odi Stadium Microsoft Teams

title.rendered: Vandalism and cable theft at Temba Waste Water Treatment Works threatens service delivery

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                          15 February 2024

Cllr Themba Fosi

MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination

The City of Tshwane strongly condemns the recent acts of vandalism and theft at Temba Waste Water Treatment Works (WWTW).

On 12 February 2024, there was a reported case of cable theft and vandalism of panels at the Temba inlet works, resulting in an estimated cost of R250 000 in damages. Subsequently on 14 February 2024, another incident of cable theft and further vandalism of panels was reported, with an estimated cost of R150 000. These incidents speak to the need for increased infrastructure security. We must work together as the City with communities and the private sector to stop these criminal syndicates.

Cable theft and vandalism are a major financial burden on the City’s already stretched budget and jeopardise the functionality of essential infrastructure that is key for service delivery to our communities.

Temba WWTW plays a vital role in ensuring the cleanliness and safety of our water supply, and any disruption to its operations can have serious consequences for our residents.

The City recognises the importance of community engagements in assisting to prevent such criminality from occurring in future. We urge anyone with information on these incidents to come forward and assist law enforcement authorities with their investigations. We are committed to fostering partnerships with residents, community organisations and businesses to establish a network of vigilant stakeholders who can help monitor and safeguard critical infrastructure facilities like Temba WWTW.

Together, we can combat vandalism and theft, ensuring the continued operation and integrity of essential public utilities for the benefit of all residents.

The City remains committed to ensuring the safety and security of its infrastructure and will continue to work diligently to address this issue and safeguard the interests of our residents.

Enquiries: Tsebo Majoro (tseboma@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: Mamelodi capital project Lusaka Clinic on track for completion this financial year

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                          15 February 2024

Cllr Rina Marx

MMC for Health

Earlier this week, I conducted a follow-up oversight visit to the construction site of the new Lusaka Clinic in Mamelodi.

This visit was in keeping with my commitment made in January 2024 to visit the site every two weeks to track progress and intervene where needed. As previously indicated, delays resulted in a revised timeline for the completion of the project, which is now the end of May 2024.

I am happy to report that since my last visit on 30 January 2024, work on the ceiling has commenced, the air conditioning is being installed, and tiling, plumbing and painting work have also commenced.

To mitigate the risk of further delays to the project, the City of Tshwane Health Department project team, along with professional service providers, are undertaking weekly site monitoring to ensure that the contract terms are adhered to and remain on track for the May 2024 completion. This is a part of the recovery plan instituted by the Health Department for the main contractor to mitigate the risk of further delays. Overall, the cumulative construction progress is assessed to be at 92%.

To date, the project has created 60 temporary employment opportunities. The clinic will be a flagship project for the City of Tshwane as it will be the first green clinic of its kind. Lusaka Clinic was designed around the green building principles, including central courtyards to bring in fresh air, and water storage and external shading to reduce heat transfer, among others.

The clinic will render comprehensive primary healthcare services to the community of Mamelodi Ext 22 and adjacent areas.

MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination

The City of Tshwane wishes to address the current situation regarding the water supply in the Mabopane area, specifically in Block C and D.

The water team was engaged in urgent repair work in Mabopane Block D to address a significant leak. Unfortunately, during these repair efforts an electricity cable was inadvertently damaged.

We have notified Eskom of the situation and our teams are standing by to commence repair work as soon as they have safely switched off the electricity supply in the area. We appreciate the patience and understanding of residents during this time.

As a result of this unforeseen circumstance, residents in Block C and D may experience disruptions to their water supply. We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience caused.

To mitigate the impact on affected residents, the City has deployed water tankers to provide interim water supply services in the affected area. We understand the importance of access to clean water and are working diligently to restore normal service as soon as possible.

Despite assurances from Eskom to dispatch a team, we regret to inform residents that the assistance has not yet arrived. We are in constant communication with Eskom to expedite the resolution process.

The City remains committed to restoring normal water supply as soon as possible and will provide updates as the situation progresses.

title.rendered: Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant pump repaired and running

The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce that the second pump at Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant (WTP) that was taken for repairs at the weekend has been returned and started running from the early hours of this morning. The City wishes to apologise once more to the affected residents for the inconvenience endured and expresses gratitude for their patience.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane requests the National Treasury to restrict Rooiwal suppliers

content.rendered:
Media statement

2 February 2024

On 1 February 2024, the City Manager of the City of Tshwane, Johann Mettler, submitted a request to the National Treasury of the Republic of South Africa to restrict the NJR Projects and Blackhead Consulting companies, which were contracted for Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant upgrades, from the central database of suppliers.

“At my discretion as an accounting officer and in line with the relevant legislation, I have requested Treasury to impose restrictions on the said companies as well as their directors to prohibit them, as suppliers, from doing business with the public sector,” said Mettler.

The City concedes that the imposition is overdue, however, there were issues of legal compliance that had to be finalised before requesting the National Treasury to effect the restrictions.

In order to speed up service delivery and in relation to the provision of clean and safe drinking water to our communities, the City has entered into a partnership with the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) to secure funding to implement upgrades to Rooiwal Phase 2.

The memorandum of understanding entered into by the two institutions details the expansion, refurbishment and upgrading of waste treatment plants, especially Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant, which needs urgent attention.

According to the City Manager, “[a]nother key factor in the partnership with DBSA is its appointment as the implementing agent for the Rooiwal Project. This will address delays in the project and ensure improved quality of life for our residents.”

“The restriction of the suppliers in question is a clear indication that the City is serious about infrastructure development in Hammanskraal, while in observance of the rules in the ongoing investigation of the Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant Project by the Special Investigating Unit and the Hawks. We will continue to give our full support to the investigating agencies,” concluded Mettler.

 Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: Executive Mayor of Tshwane conducts service delivery oversight visits in Hammanskraal and Mamelodi

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                            30 January 2024

Cllr Cilliers Brink

Executive Mayor of Tshwane

Earlier today, I conducted a service delivery oversight visit in Hammanskraal in Region 2. This forms part of our drive to ensure the successful implementation of our Urban Management Plan. As regularly communicated, our Urban Management Plan focuses on key routes within regions, including public spaces such as parks and key buildings.

In Hammanskraal today, our teams on the ground delivered basic services such as cutting grass, patching potholes and fixing street lights. I also had the opportunity to engage with regional staff and management who highlighted challenges faced by employees, including operational issues, such as an overreliance on contractors. These conversations are important, especially as we go into the budget planning cycle.

I have also been to Mamelodi on Monday to conduct an oversight visit to the Mamelodi R3 and R4 Reservoirs. This in response to the water supply challenges affecting many of our residents.

Our teams are working towards ensuring a stable supply of water for all residents. As of this morning, 30 January 2024, our reservoir levels were improving with Mamelodi R3 Reservoir at 52% and Mamelodi R4 Reservoir at 29%. While increasing reservoir levels is promising news, the main issue is still illegal connections to our water systems by informal settlements.

The reality is that there is an increasing number of land invasions near our Mamelodi reservoirs. This has led to high levels of illegal connections on the water distribution network, which interrupts water supply to law-abiding residents who diligently pay their rates and taxes.

In response to this issue, the City is working on a plan to safeguard the water supply infrastructure and ensure uninterrupted access to clean and safe water for all residents in Mamelodi and broader areas.

We apologise to the affected residents for the water supply challenges.

siphost@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: City of Tshwane intensifies efforts to fight illegal electricity and water connections

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                            26 January 2023

Cllr Themba Fosi

MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination

The City of Tshwane is intensifying efforts to combat the detrimental impact of illegal utility connections on the municipality’s revenue and the provision of essential services. The prevalence of unauthorised electricity and water connections compromises the integrity of the City’s utility systems and hampers equitable access to services for those who diligently contribute to the City by paying their rates.

Illegal utility connections undermine the financial stability of the municipality, impeding our capacity to invest in essential infrastructure and maintain the high standard of services our residents deserve. This unlawful practice places an undue burden on households, businesses and law-abiding citizens who faithfully fulfil their financial obligations to the City.

In recognition of the severity of this issue, the City of Tshwane, in collaboration with law enforcement authorities, including the Tshwane Metro Police Department (TMPD) and the South African Police Service (SAPS), have implemented stringent measures to identify, address and eradicate illegal utility connections. The enforcement of these measures is crucial to safeguard the integrity of our utility networks, preserve revenue streams and ensure the sustainable delivery of services to our residents.

We extend our sincere appreciation to the responsible and law-abiding residents of Tshwane who consistently fulfil their civic duty by paying their rates. Your commitment is instrumental in supporting the continued improvement of our communities and the provision of essential services.

To amplify our impact on the battle against illegal utility connections, we call upon our residents to actively engage with us in this crucial undertaking. By fostering a sense of collective responsibility, we can protect our City from the adverse effects of illegal connections and preserve the quality of services for everyone.

Residents are encouraged to report any suspicious or unauthorised utility connections to the City on 012 358 7095/7096 or Eskom on 08600 37566.Top of Form

title.rendered: Tshwane Council approves Rooiwal and Pretoria West power stations leasing report following a successful public participation process.

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                  25 January 2024
Cllr Cilliers Brink
Executive Mayor of Tshwane

Today, the City of Tshwane Council approved the second Rooiwal report, which gives the green light to procced with the 40-year lease of Rooiwal Power Station and Pretoria West Power Station in terms of Regulation 35 of the Municipal Asset Transfer Regulations.

This follows our robust public participation engagements with various stakeholders wherein we received an overwhelming positive response which indicates that our residents understand that we need to take drastic actions to end load-shedding for an energy secure future.

Today’s Council approval is one of the six steps to get the two power stations running again. It marks a major milestone to move Tshwane closer to energy independence and stabilising electricity supply to communities.

As part of our master energy plan, over the next three years, the City working towards securing at least 1 000 MW of alternative energy. This has occasioned the need for the City to engage with independent power producers and open up opportunities for alternative energy production.

So far, we are pleased with the transparent manner in which the leasing process is unfolding. Additionally, given the scale of the transaction, the City Manager will appoint a professional transactional advisory team to ensure maximum effectiveness.

Tshwane residents should be proud of this progressive step because every time higher stages of load-shedding hit us, it destroys our infrastructure, leads to prolonged outages and frustration, and creates opportunities for cable theft. That is why this project to move in a different direction is so important for our future.

I want to reiterate that the leasing process will not favour any specific energy provider and will be managed in a transparent, competitive, and fair manner. I look forward to announcing other initiatives as part of our energy plan to reduce the City’s dependence on Eskom and alleviate the burden of load-shedding for all our residents.

Media enquiries: Sipho Stuurman
(siphost@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: City of Tshwane remains on alert to possible cholera outbreak

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                            15 January 2024

Cllr Rina Marx

MMC for Health

With the anticipation of community members returning after travelling during the festive period and the reopening of factories and schools, the City of Tshwane Health Department is on high alert to manage a possible cholera outbreak.

Cholera is contracted through water or food contaminated with the cholera bacteria (vibrio cholera) and early treatment is critical. Community members are urged to immediately present to their nearest healthcare facility if any of the following symptoms are experienced:

  • Watery diarrhoea
  • Rice water like appearance of stools
  • Nausea and vomiting
  • Muscle cramps

Preventative plans, including health education, were already implemented prior to the festive period and will continue. To date, no cases have been reported, however, outbreak response teams inclusive of municipal health teams and community workers are ready to respond if the need arises.

The department’s efforts remain focused on preventative measures and good hand hygiene is important to prevent the spread of cholera. Please be vigilant of any feeling of unwellness and visit your nearest healthcare facilities.

Remember to wash your hands with soap and water all the time and drink lots of safe water to prevent dehydration.

Media enquiries:

Natashia Chhiba

(natashiach@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: City of tshwane refutes false allegations published in City press newspaper about an irregular r4 billion water tender award

content.rendered:
Media statement

 City of tshwane refutes false allegations published in City press newspaper about an irregular r4 billion water tender award

 18 December 2023

The City Press newspaper, in its edition of Sunday, 17 December 2023, published a Page 2 lead article headlined “R4BN WATER TANKER TENDER CONTROVERSY” which contained a litany of falsehoods, distortions and fabrications.

On the afternoon of Thursday, 7 December 2023, City Press journalist Mr Norman Masungwini sent the City of Tshwane an incredibly long list of 22 questions about alleged shenanigans in the water tender award, with a deadline for the next day at 10:00. Despite the media enquiry requiring the arduous task of delving into the archives to retrieve the relevant information, all the questions were responded to on Friday, 8 December 2023. For reasons best known to City Press, they selectively and subjectively ignored answers which did not suit their perspective.

The City denies that the tender is worth R4 billion. The estimated value of the tender for the appointment of service providers for the hire of 10 000 ℓ mobile drinking water tankers (trucks) to supply informal settlements in Tshwane for a period of three years, as and when required, is R1 billion over the next three years.

The City only budgeted approximately R262 million for the 2022/23 financial year. This information was communicated to the journalist, but he stuck to the manufactured amount of R4 billion. This tender (HHS 05-2022/23) was never set aside by the Pretoria High Court. In fact, the City gave regular reports to the High Court regarding all its endeavours and processes leading up to the award of this tender. Needless to say, everything about this tender award was above board.

The City of Tshwane management did not overrule the resolution of the Bid Evaluation Committee and the Bid Adjudication Committee on the matter. It was made clear to Mr Masungwini that the City has obtained two legal opinions from Senior Counsel to inform decision-making. However, to our surprise, he did not consider this information when publishing the story.

Yes, it is true that, on 28 November 2022, the High Court (North Gauteng Division) issued an order against the City of Tshwane, saying that the award of the tender for the appointment of service providers for provision of rudimentary water services to informal settlements, as and when required, for the next three years (HHS 01-2021/22) should be set aside, based on the tender validity period having lapsed at the time of its award. The case involved Aptitude Trading Enterprise (Pty) Ltd, Mdoseni Trading & Projects (Pty) Ltd and LTC Holding CC, who made a court application seeking that the tender award be reviewed and set aside due to its validity having expired at the time that it was awarded.

The appointment of the current tender was based on the legal counsel provided. The City launched investigations based on the recommendations of the probity report and allegations that various Supply Chain Management Division officials are implicated in the tender where bidders were compelled to pay bribes in exchange for being awarded the tender.

The Bid Adjudication Committee never noted that the contract has been declared invalid by the court and requested that it be cancelled. The tender (HHS 05-2022/23) for the appointment of service providers for the hire of 10 000 ℓ mobile drinking water tankers (trucks) to supply in informal settlements in Tshwane for a period of three years, as and when required, was never invalidated by a court. It appears that the journalist conflated tender HHS 01‑2021/22) with tender HHS 05-2022/23. We hope that this was not deliberate and that he was not pushing a sponsored narrative.

The City did not advertise any secondary tender to prevent a fight, as asserted in the article. As pointed out to the journalist, in writing, the envisaged secondary tender procurement process was to augment the shortfall in the number of trucks presented by the current tender.

Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane on high alert following cholera outbreak in Zimbabwe

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                       13 December 2023

Cllr Rina Marx

MMC for Health

The national Department of Health has issued an advisory calling for preparedness in South Africa amid the ongoing outbreak of cholera in neighbouring countries, most notably Zimbabwe.

Given that cross-border travel is expected to increase due to the festive season, the City of Tshwane Health Department would like to encourage residents to take the necessary precautions.

Cholera is contracted through water or food contaminated with the cholera bacteria (vibrio cholera). Symptoms include watery diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, dehydration and muscle cramps. These can be treated with intravenous fluids to hydrate and antibiotics. Early treatment is critical.

If you are unsure about the quality of water, boil water before use. Wash fruit, vegetables and meat using water that has been boiled. Good hand hygiene is important to prevent the spread of cholera.

The City of Tshwane Health Department has already put measures in place to ensure a speedy response to possible cholera cases.

  • Clinical staff have been alerted to remain vigilant and follow relevant protocols if community members present with watery diarrhoea at clinics.
  • A communication team will share cholera preventative e-cards on social media platforms.
  • Newly appointed peer educators are in the process of receiving in-service training, including several health promotion and educational messages.
  • Municipal health services teams are ready to respond to requests for water quality

Though the department’s efforts remain focused on preventative measures, our outbreak response teams are ready should they be required. Cholera is highly preventable and treatable if detected early. Please be vigilant.

Media enquiries: Natashia Chhiba (natashiach@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: City of Tshwane launches Bronkhorstbaai Water Treatment Plan

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                        8 December 2023

Cllr Themba Fosi

MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination

The City of Tshwane is delighted to announce the successful launch of Bronkhorstbaai Water Treatment Plant, a significant milestone in our commitment to providing clean and safe water to the community.

This water treatment plant marks the culmination of extensive planning, engineering and collaborative efforts to enhance water infrastructure in the region. This state-of-the-art facility is a testament to our dedication to stable water supply and ensuring the well-being of the communities we serve.

This water treatment plant project has addressed the imperative need of improving water quality by increasing capacity from 120 kℓ to 1 500 kℓ. The existing plant, having reached the end of its life cycle, necessitated the installation of a new treatment plant (package plant), a new abstraction point, a pump house, a 1 500 kℓ clear water tank, a new 1 500 kℓ reservoir at Bronkhorstbaai low level and the installation of a bulk pipeline with chambers.

The project had a positive impact on employment and local businesses. A total of 22 Expanded Public Works Programme beneficiaries, comprising five males, five females, ten male youths and two female youths, were appointed. Additionally, seven small, medium and micro enterprises were engaged, resulting in a local expenditure of R7,9 million.

Furthermore, we are thrilled to announce a unique opportunity for young graduates to gain exposure and hands-on experience at Bronkhorstbaai Water Treatment Plant. As part of our commitment to fostering local talent and contributing to community development, we are initiating a programme that invites young professionals to work closely with the plant manager to understand and contribute to the plant’s daily operations. This initiative aims to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical application, empowering the youth with crucial skills for the sustainable management of water treatment facilities.

Looking ahead, we are excited to announce that the second phase of this initiative will extend to the Nkangala area, reinforcing our commitment to comprehensive water management and community empowerment.

The City expresses gratitude to all stakeholders, partners and the community for their unwavering support throughout the development and launch of Bronkhorstbaai Water Treatment Plant. As we celebrate this achievement, we urge the community to take pride in this essential infrastructure and contribute to its sustainable operation by curbing vandalism and theft.

Enquiries: MMC Themba Fosi (thembamandlaf@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: Reminder: City of Tshwane urges residents to conserve water as its water storage system is severely under pressure due to high water consumption

content.rendered:
Media statement

 8 December 2023

 The City of Tshwane is currently facing a significant challenge with its water storage system due to high water consumption in some parts of the city. This has put immense strain on the water reservoir system.

The soaring hot temperatures have also contributed to a substantial increase in water use and consumption by residents, pushing the reservoir levels to drop significantly. In light of this, the City pleads with all Tshwane residents to use water sparingly and take practical measures aimed at preventing the total depletion of water in its reservoirs.

Some of the areas that have been flagged to be contributing to the high consumption are the following:

  1. Doringkloof Reservoir which feeds Brakfontein 390-JR, Doornkloof 391-JR, Doringkloof, Doringkloof Ext 1, Die Hoewes Ext 104, 129, 212, 249, 264 and 311, Highveld (all extensions), Highveld Technopark, Irene (all extensions), Lyttelton 381-JR, Lyttelton AH Ext 1, Lyttelton Manor, Lyttelton Manor Ext 3, 5 and 11, and Zwartkop Ext 8 and 26

  12. Parkmore HL and LL Reservoirs which feeds Alphen Park, Ashlea Gardens, Constantia Park (all extensions), De Beers, Faerie Glen (all extensions), Garsfontein (all extensions), Lynnwood Glen, Lynnwood Park, Maroelana, Menlyn, Newlands (all extensions), Pretoriuspark (all extensions), Tshwane, Valley Farm 379-JR, Waterkloof Glen (all extensions) and Waterkloof Park
  13. Queenswood Reservoir which feeds Colbyn, Deerness, Koedoespoort, Koedoespoort 325-JR, Môregloed, Queenswood, Rietfontein, Rietfontein 321-JR, Rietondale, Villieria and Waverley
  14. Rosslyn North Reservoir which feeds Klipfontein 268-JR, Klip-Kruisfontein 708-JR, Soshanguve A, B, TT, VV and XX, Soshanguve South (all extensions), Haakdoornboom 267-JR, Kruisfontein 259-JR, Kruisfontein 262-JR, Soshanguve East and Soshanguve South Ext 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14
  15. Saulsville Reservoir which feeds Atteridgeville (all extensions), Atteridgeville 607-JR, Elandsfontein 352-JR, Pretoria Town and Townlands 351-JR and Saulsville
  16. Sinoville HL and LL Reservoirs which feeds Sinoville (all extensions)
  17. Soshanguve Reservoir which feeds De Beers, Kopanong, Kopanong Ext 1, Kruisfontein 259-JR, Kruisfontein 262-JR, Mabopane Block S, Onderstepoort Ext 33, Onderstepoort 266-JR, Rietgat 611-JR, Soshanguve Block AA, BB, CC, DD, MM, TT, UU, VV, WW and ZZ, Soshanguve Block F, G, H, K, L, L Ext 0 and M, Soshanguve East (all extensions), Soshanguve South Ext 1 and 2, The Farm 670-JR and Wentzelrust 223-JR

The excessive use of water during this heatwave has resulted in a critical situation where the City’s reservoirs are under immense stress. If this trend continues, it could potentially lead to water shortages and a compromised water supply to the residents.

The City understands that the heatwave has created a need for increased water use, particularly for personal hygiene, hydration and other essential purposes. However, residents are urged to adopt water-saving practices in their daily routine.

By implementing small changes in water-consumption habits, the City of Tshwane and Tshwane residents can collectively make a significant impact on conserving water and safeguarding the reservoir system.

Here are some practical steps residents can take to contribute to water-conservation efforts:

  • Do not water or irrigate gardens with hosepipes or sprinkler systems between 06:00 and 18:00.
  • Do not wash cars using a hosepipe.
  • Do not clean driveways or pavements using a hosepipe.
  • Flush toilets only when necessary.
  • Close a running tap while brushing teeth.
  • Reduce daily water use as much as possible.
  • Fix water leaks in your yard and report street leaks. Even small leaks can contribute to significant water wastage over time.
  • Do not fill swimming pools from the municipal water supply. Manually topping up swimming pools is allowed only if the swimming pool is fitted with a pool cover that prevents evaporation.

Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane hosts Entrepreneurship Day in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                       21 November 2023

Ald Hannes Coetzee

MMC for Economic Development and Spatial Planning

The City of Tshwane, in collaboration with the Small Enterprise Development Agency (SEDA), hosted an Entrepreneurship Day in Hammanskraal, showcasing our commitment to supporting local businesses and fostering economic growth within townships.

The event, which commenced on Friday, 17 November 2023, was a resounding success, featuring a seminar attended by 110 entrepreneurs and aspirant entrepreneurs. The seminar aimed to equip aspiring and existing entrepreneurs with valuable knowledge, insights and resources to help them thrive in their respective industries. Participants had the opportunity to learn from industry experts, engage in interactive sessions and gain the practical skills necessary for business development and growth.

The seminar was followed by a colourful pop-up market in Hammanskraal Stadium on 18 November 2023, transforming the stadium into a busy hub of entrepreneurial activity. We were happy to give a venue for 44 local small, medium and micro-sized enterprises (SMMEs) to show and sell their distinctive products to a willing audience. The pop-up market provided these SMMEs with not just direct sales but also publicity, brand awareness and crucial contacts within the community.

By leveraging the long-standing partnership between SEDA and the City of Tshwane, these collaborative efforts can create a vibrant entrepreneurial ecosystem, promote economic growth and empower aspiring and existing entrepreneurs in the region. It is through events like the Entrepreneurship Day that we strive to celebrate the resilience, ingenuity and contributions of our local businesses, while also fostering an environment conducive to their growth and success.

We extend our sincere gratitude to all the role players, participants and partners who made this event possible. We also extend our appreciation to the community of Hammanskraal for their support and engagement throughout the event.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane receives Public Protector Hammanskraal water report, remedial actions already being implemented

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                          1 November 2023

Cllr Cilliers Brink

Executive Mayor of Tshwane

I welcome the report of the Public Protector into the Hammanskraal water crisis and commit to the remedial actions that have been ordered. As I have said at the outset of my term of office, the dysfunctionality of Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant is a stain on the conscience of the City, including various administrations.

The Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant is hydraulically and organically overloaded, so it pollutes the Apies River and the downstream water supply. If the plant had been upgraded in the first decade of this century, as the City’s masterplan recommended in 2004, then enormous expense and suffering might have been avoided.

While the City cannot change what happened in the past, we can learn from it and take responsibility for redressing the problem. The remedial actions ordered by the Public Protector accords with what the City has already undertaken in partnership with the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS). That partnership agreement is being monitored by the Mayoral Committee, and a full report in compliance with the Public Protector remedial actions will be tabled at the municipal Council before the end of this month.

The City has allocated R450 million towards upgrading Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant over a three-year period. This includes R150 million spread over each financial year. Priority will be given to finalise Phase 1 upgrades and to initiate Phase 2 upgrades.

Our partnership with the DWS will be essential to our success, as will the continued funding of capital projects by the national government. As previously communicated, the Development Bank of South Africa will act as an independent implementing agent and on our part as the City we maintain that no companies implicated in                 corruption or in state capture are awarded any tenders.

We must now all work together to provide a long-lasting solution for the benefit of the people of Hammanskraal. The City will study the further particulars of the report and ensure that we deliver on our promise to the people of Hammanskraal.

Media enquiries:  Sipho Stuurman

(siphost@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: Tampering with critical gas and water infrastructure can lead to a disastrous outcome

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                            30 October 2023

Ald Grandi Theunissen

MMC for Community Safety

It has come to the attention of the Tshwane Emergency Services Department that some unknown vandals temper with Rand Water and SASOL water and gas pipelines markings in Sekampaneng Ridge near Suurman in Hamanskraal. It is alleged that the infrastructure is vandalised for theft of ferrous metals.

The risks associated with the destruction of high-pressure water and gas lines, as well as electricity infrastructure, are severe and may lead to catastrophic outcomes, including flooding, explosions, loss of life, and significant property damage. It can also cause prolonged power outages and water shortages.

We therefore urge residents to refrain from vandalizing infrastructure belonging to SASOL, Rand Water, and any other vital service providers. Community members are strongly encouraged to promptly report any instances of infrastructure vandalism to their local police station or notify relevant authorities. You can reach SASOL at 0800 212 260, Rand Water at 0860 10 10 60, Eskom via 0800 112 722, and TMPD’s Cable Theft Unit via 012 358 1550.

By working together and taking collective responsibility, we can prevent major incidents such as the recent gas explosion in the Johannesburg CBD and the burst water pipe in Mamelodi in August 2012.

The coalition government in the City of Tshwane is fully committed to safeguarding our vital infrastructure. Let’s stand together in protecting our community’s safety and well-being.

Should an incident occur however, residents in need of Emergency Services are reminded to call them toll free via 107. Residents in need of the Gauteng Ambulance Service can call 10177 from a landline (toll free) or 112 from a cellular phone (toll free).

Enquiries: Ald Grandi Theunissen

Cllr Ofentse Madzebatela

MMC for Human Settlements

I am pleased to report that the sampled water carried through mobile water tankers in New Eersterus in Hammanskraal complies with the SANS241:2015 water standards and is safe to drink.

The City’s microbiologists in the Water and Sanitation Department’s Scientific Services Section conducted random unannounced tests on five mobile waters and their extraction points recently and published the results of the tests within the assured seven days.

The results came back with 100% compliance for applicable standards.

These microbiology tests checked foreign elements such as ammonia phosphate and nitrates and checked the PH levels of the water.

The tested mobile water tankers deliver water to the areas of Spin City, Trust Farm, Phophola, Phomolong, Hammanskraal Ext 2, Kanana, Nkandla, Chris Hani Block G, Kudube Unit 10, Hammanskraal Portion 9, New Eersterust Ext 8, Marikana and Soutpan.

The City is working on a long-term plan to have a tap in every household. While this process is underway, we will continue to conduct announced tests in all regions of Tshwane to ensure that our residents receive only the highest quality of water through mobile tankers.

I would like to thank the microbiologist team for their swift response and the diligent work they have done in eliminating fears of inferior water being provided to the public.

The provision of clean and quality water remains a priority of the multiparty government.
