title.rendered: Tshwane Health Department cautions against misinformation regarding the source of the Hammanskraal cholera outbreak

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                            27 October 2023

Cllr Rina Marx

MMC for Health

The City of Tshwane Health Department has noted with concern recent messages in circulation on social media indicating that the source of the recent cholera outbreak in Hammanskraal can be traced to Rooiwal Wastewater Treatment Plant and that the City of Tshwane bears culpability.

The cholera outbreak prompted a multidisciplinary intervention between local, provincial and national government. Water testing efforts of various sources were ramped up, including taps, water tankers, boreholes, bottled water, rivers and streams.

The City of Tshwane Health Department would like to reaffirm that the national Department of Water and Sanitation commissioned the Water Research Commission to undertake an independent investigation into the cholera outbreak.

The investigations included, among others, microbiologists, epidemiologists and engineers to assess the functionality and compliance of waste management systems. In addition, laboratories accredited by the South African National Accreditation System were brought on board to test samples for toxigenic vibrio cholera and other bacteria. The findings of the independent investigation in July 2023 concluded that it remains unknown whether water was a source of the cholera outbreak.

As the MMC responsible for Health, I would like to caution residents against spreading disinformation from unverified sources. This has the potential to create unnecessary panic among communities.

Our Health department remains committed to executing its municipal health services mandate which includes monitoring water quality and availability. This work includes water sampling, testing, and mapping water sources in relation to pollution and contamination and protecting water sources.

Enquiries: Natashia Chhiba (natashiach@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: City of Tshwane celebrates elderly club in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                            24 October 2023

Cllr Peggy de Bruin

MMC for Community and Social Development Services

 The City of Tshwane congratulates Gogo Christina Sepale on being selected to represent Gauteng in the Provincial Active Ageing Games scheduled to take place in Mbombela. The senior citizen games are hosted annually to promote an active ageing, healthy lifestyle and social integration among elderly people.

Gogo Christina is a member of the Rockville Gogo’s Project Club in Hammanskraal. The club was founded in 2015 by Ms Francina Nawa, another elder in the community. Soccer is one of the activities that the club is engaged in where they compete with other soccer teams in neighbouring townships.

The City has been supporting the club since its inception through registering an NPO certificate, by-law compliance, business and administrative skills as well as a food security programme. Other activities include gardening and sewing.

With the assistance of donors and good Samaritans, the club managed to build a four-room house in order to manage their daily operations. To sustain the club, the elders contribute R50 each monthly towards club expenses.

It is important for elders as it is for any person to be physically active and take part in exercise to prolong their quality of life. We wish many other elders of Tshwane can take part in Active-Ageing Programmes similar to Rockville Gogo’s Project Club.

title.rendered: Four suspects arrested for malicious damage to property and intimidation

content.rendered:
Media statement

 23 October 2023

The City of Tshwane would like to commend the swift action by law enforcement agencies for the arrest of four suspects accused of pelting three Tshwane Bus Services (TBS) buses with stones in different parts of the city today.

The buses were damaged in Belle Ombre, Pretoria North and outside the C De Wet Bus Depot in the Pretoria CBD. One suspect was found in possession of a bag full of stones. The arrests were a result of a multidisciplinary operation undertaken jointly by the South African Police Service (SAPS) Dog Unit and Tshwane Metro Police Department (TMPD) aimed at curbing criminality that has characterised the unlawful and unprotected strike by some employees of the City.

The suspects are facing charges of malicious damage to property and intimidation. The TBS resumed operations this morning after almost three months of absence owing to some employees who participated in the strike action, which was declared unlawful and unprotected by the Labour Court in July 2023.

The court subsequently granted the City a permanent interdict against the striking employees in September 2023.

This morning, the TBS operated 36 of the 160 daily shifts. The majority of drivers reported for duty but refused to drive the buses. Internal processes are underway to deal with employees who refused to execute their duties today.

City management is adamant that the bus services will not be withdrawn amid the intimidation and will instead beef up security to protect the bus drivers, our valued commuters and the bus fleet.

The SAPS and TMPD have vowed to clamp down harshly on anyone who intimidates non-striking employees and those who partake in acts of violence. Law enforcement agencies are on alert around all the routes operated by the TBS and at the depots.

 Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: Update on power supply to Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works

content.rendered:
Media statement
12 October 2023

Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works (WWTW) is now ready for operational

optimisation following the successful power switch from the Bon Accord Power Line to
the newly rebuilt Pyramid Substation today.

Pyramid Substation was successfully rebuilt in just 18 days after it was damaged by
fire, which was caused by severe storms that swept through parts of the city last
month. The rebuilding project, which was completed within the projected schedule,
involved demolishing the damaged structure, panels, feeder cables, circuit breakers,
132 kV isolator and key transformer components.

During the rebuilding process, the power supply to Rooiwal WWTW was temporarily
rerouted from a refurbished, previously underused power line from Bon Accord. The
power has now been switched back to the original supply from Pyramid Substation
after the City’s technicians confirmed that the electricity at the substation is stable.

Aeration required for the biological treatment of waste water will be started in
phases under the supervision of a contractor due to the sensitivity of the specialised
equipment.

The full restoration and operation of all infrastructure at Rooiwal WWTW is receiving
the necessary attention to ensure the continuous treatment of waste water.

Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: Rooiwal Power Station update: Significant progress made at Pyramid Substation

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                              5 October 2023

Cllr Themba Fosi

MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination

The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce substantial progress at Pyramid Substation. The City has been diligently working on-site to assess the extent of the damage and undertake necessary repair and restoration efforts. Repairs reached a significant milestone with several critical components nearing completion.

Approximately 85% of the cable work is completed, with 630 incomer cable terminations successfully completed. Panel 5, featuring 150 cable feeders to the water treatment plant, has undergone cable jointing and termination. All 150 m2 of feeder cables are now connected and terminated. All 240 m2 of feeder cables have been connected and terminated, marking a substantial achievement.

The installation of the 132 kV circuit breaker is now complete. Our dedicated team is currently engaged in the meticulous task of multicore and control cable installation for the breaker. The installation of the 132 kV isolator is completed, enhancing the reliability and safety of the Rooiwal infrastructure.

Pertaining to the transformer auxiliary, the installation of the NEC (National Electrical Code) is now complete. Rigorous testing of the NEC has been carried out and successfully finalised.

The following significant progress has been made regarding the transformer:

  • Key transformer components, including bushings, have been expertly installed
  • Oil purification, a vital step in the process, has been effectively completed
  • Single cores have been successfully integrated into the system
  • Our dedicated team is currently working on the installation of multicore and control cables for the transformer
  • Tomorrow, the team is planning to energise the transformer, allowing it to soak before it takes on its full load, ensuring a seamless transition

The installation of the 11 kV switchgear panels is now complete. A critical bus bar pressure testing process has been conducted and tested positive, ensuring the utmost reliability.

Our team is actively engaged in the installation of multicores for the 132 kV protection panel. Cold commissioning is in progress, marking another crucial step in the project’s advancement.

The installation of batteries and the associated charger is now fully completed. Comprehensive testing of these components has been successfully concluded, ensuring their readiness for operation.

The remaining work includes AC installation to the building which stands at 0%, and this task will be addressed in the upcoming phases of the project.

The City of Tshwane is committed to ensuring the timely restoration of Pyramid Substation and the resumption of normal power supply to the affected areas. We appreciate the patience of our residents during this process and assure you that all efforts are being made to expedite the completion of the necessary work.

Enquiries: MMC Themba Fosi (thembamandlaf@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: Major development plans for old Pretoria showgrounds in the pipeline

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                              3 October 2023

Cllr Kingsley Wakelin

MMC for Corporate and Shared Services

The City of Tshwane has grand plans to turn the old Pretoria showgrounds into a commercial mixed-use precinct with a hotel and conferencing, retail, office and residential opportunities.

In June 2022, Council gave approval for the showgrounds to be put out on an open and competitive bidding process to any developer who will lease it and realise the City’s vision for the property. This lease will be a 50-year term to allow developers to make significant investments in the property that would benefit the City and its residents for years to come.

To make the property attractive to developers, the City is busy with consolidation and rezoning processes to get the best bids possible. Development will then take place as soon as the winning developer is announced. The bidding process will be open and fair, and no trace of corruption will be tolerated. This development must be above board and in the best interest of residents at all times.

These plans are envisioned to turn the showgrounds into a leading events venue that unlocks the development potential of the property and provides much-needed economic development and job opportunities for Tshwane residents.

It must be noted that between 1995 and 2021 the property was under the management of the Tshwane Business and Agricultural Corporation, which unfortunately allowed it to fall into ruin, forcing us to take the property back to save it from further decay.

Currently, the property is being guarded by private security companies contracted to the City. These companies have been negligent in their duties, which has resulted in littering and vandalism on the property. The City will put the security companies on terms to revise their guards and beef up security so that the showgrounds remain an attractive and viable investment opportunity.

Furthermore, we will start with refurbishments to prepare the property for short-term rentals. This will help the City derive some benefits while the consolidation and rezoning processes conclude, as these can take more than a year.

One of the potential rentals is the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC), who have shown interest in using the property as a base for the 2024 general elections and leasing a portion of the property long term for the 2026 local government elections. We welcome the IEC’s proposal and are committed to making it happen.

I would like to invite all interested developers to reach out to Group Property with any queries and to look out for the publishing of the tender.

We are determined to unlock all development potential in the City to promote economic growth and job opportunities and make the City of Tshwane a City that works for all.

Enquiries:

MMC Kingsley Wakelin

kingsleysw@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: Public participation process to lease Rooiwal Power Station and Pretoria West Power Station is open for public comments

content.rendered:
Media statement
Cllr Cilliers Brink
Executive Mayor of Tshwane

28 September 2023

I would like to encourage our residents and all interested stakeholders to take part in
the City’s public participation process for the proposed 40-year lease of Rooiwal Power
Station and Pretoria West Power Station in terms of Regulation 35 of the Municipal
Asset Transfer Regulations.

This comes after the City of Tshwane Council, on 12 September 2023, approved a
public participation report for the proposed leasing of the two power stations.
Getting the public’s input is a crucial first step in our energy master plan for Tshwane,
which seeks to reduce the City’s dependence on Eskom and alleviate the burden of
load shedding.

A positive outcome of the public participation process and the subsequent Council
endorsement will unlock much needed electricity-generating capacity at both power
stations in order to benefit our communities.

Rooiwal Power Station has been dormant for almost a decade, and using it again will
reduce the burden of load shedding on our communities.
Written comments can be submitted by email to verusham@tshwane.gov.za or
delivered at Room 105, 1st Floor, Ou Raadsaal Building, Church Square, Pretoria. All
written comments must be submitted on or before 31 October 2023.

Copies of the Council resolution pertaining to the lease can be accessed on the City’s
website (https://www.tshwane.gov.za/?page_id=6652) and at our Tshwane customer
care centres and libraries.

Enquiries can be sent to Johanna Maenetsa on 012 358 7389 or
johannahmae@tshwane.gov.za.

Reviving the two power stations is important for an energy-secure future
for our city. I also want to make it clear that this process will not favour
any specific energy provider and will be managed in a transparent,
competitive and fair manner.

Media enquiries: Sipho Stuurman (siphost@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: Tshwane Mayor welcomes investigation by Special Investigating Unit into failed  Rooiwal tender

content.rendered:
Media statement

26 September 2023

Cllr Cilliers Brink
Executive Mayor of Tshwane

On behalf of the City of Tshwane, I would like to welcome the recently announced Special
Investigating Unit (SIU) investigation into the failed tender to upgrade Rooiwal Waste Water
Treatment Plant.

This is exactly what our multiparty coalition government has been calling for: A high-level
investigation into the matter, with possible criminal charges for all tenderpreneurs who are
found to have benefitted unlawfully.

Furthermore, the SIU investigation will help us in our efforts to clean up the City’s Supply
Chain Management Division and will also assist in recovering the stolen funds which the City
needs to drive service delivery to our residents.

The joint venture CMS, NJR & Blackhead was appointed in October 2019 in respect of tender
USD WS 30-2017/18 for the construction of Phase 1 of the upgrade and refurbishment of
Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works at a cost of R291 996 799,07.

However, the joint venture failed to honour the contract and subjected the Rooiwal Phase 1
upgrades to long delays and continued non-performance, which resulted in the City
terminating the contract in August 2022.

The group only completed 60% of the Rooiwal upgrades, despite all the money spent by the
City for Phase 1. Furthermore, a forensic investigation has found that the tender had been
awarded irregularly. In this regard, disciplinary processes are underway against several City
officials who are implicated.

Following my calls to the City Manager, the City is now in the process of blacklisting the joint
venture, together with its shareholders and directors, including the state capture accused,
Edwin Sodi.

Effectively, this means that the joint venture, as well as its shareholders and
directors, will be listed by the National Treasury as restricted suppliers. This
will result in these individuals being restricted from doing or obtaining any
business with the state for a period of five years.

As Tshwane mayor, I am determined to fight corruption and to keep our original
promise to run a clean, effective, and corruption-free administration.

Media enquiries: Sipho Stuurman (siphost@tshwane.gov.za).

The City also pleads with residents who were not affected by the water outages to assist the system to stabilise speedily by using water sparingly and only when it is absolutely necessary.

The City apologises profusely to the residents who were affected by the water outages.

title.rendered: Rand Water’s Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant affected by severe thunderstorm

content.rendered:
On Thursday, 21 September 2023, Rand Water informed the City of Tshwane about their Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant that had experienced a power trip which affected production.

This follows disruptions in operations due to a severe thunderstorm that occurred around midnight on Tuesday, 19 September 2023. Attempts to restart the plant revealed faults along the overhead power lines supplying the plant.

The power failure resulted in the loss in production of 2 000 million litres of water per day. This load reduction impacted all municipalities supplied by Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant, namely the City of Tshwane, City of Ekurhuleni and City of Johannesburg, among others.

The following systems are affected:

    • Palmiet System: Klipriviersberg, Klipfontein, Brakfontein, Germiston, Northridge, Hartebeeshoek and Vlakfontein
  • Mapleton System: Brakpan, Vlakfontein, Selcourt, Wildebeestfontein, Stompiesfontein and Bronberg
  • Eikenhof System: Meredale and Waterval

The Mapleton System, which supplies mainly the eastern parts of Tshwane, has since recovered and is pumping at full load. It is important to highlight that the thunderstorm and power failure incidents occurred while the City’s and mainly Rand Water’s systems were under severe strain due to high water consumption, which exacerbates the situation.

The City urges residents to adopt water-saving measures to reduce high water consumption and avoid a total collapse of the system.

WATER-SAVING TIPS

Residents are urged to keep using grey water to water gardens and flush toilets. Residents should report water leaks, burst pipes and all incidents where water is wasted. Where possible, water-saving devices should be installed.

Furthermore, residents should make water conservation part of their everyday lives by making use of the following water-saving tips:

  • Install a low-flow shower head and tap aerators where possible.
  • Use a dual-flush toilet cistern.
  • Plant indigenous or drought-resistant shrubs in the garden.
  • Do not water or irrigate gardens with hosepipes or sprinkler systems between 06:00 and 18:00.
  • Do not wash vehicles with hosepipes.
  • Do not fill swimming pools.
  • Use a broom instead of a hosepipe when cleaning driveways or patios.
  • Collect rainwater to reuse in the garden or wash the car.
  • Cover the swimming pool to reduce water evaporation.
  • Take a shower rather than a bath.
  • Close a running tap while brushing teeth or shaving.
  • Regularly check toilets and taps for leaks.

080 1111 556

title.rendered: City of Tshwane Council approves public participation report to lease Rooiwal and Pretoria West Power Stations

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                      12 September 2023

Cllr Cilliers Brink

Executive Mayor of Tshwane 

Today, the City of Tshwane Council approved a public participation report for the proposed 40-year lease of the Rooiwal and Pretoria West Power Stations in terms of Regulation 35 of the Municipal Asset Transfer Regulations.

This an important first step in our energy master plan for Tshwane which, seeks to reduce the City’s dependence on Eskom and alleviate the burden of load-shedding.

The Council-approved report forms part of the work of our Energy Task Team, which we appointed earlier in the year to look at a mix of energy solutions for the City in the face of the ongoing load-shedding crisis.

Key to the work of the Energy Task Team are plans to revive the Rooiwal and Pretoria West Power Stations. I want to make it clear that the mandate of this task team is not to favour any one energy provider or any one method of energy generation, but to open our offer as widely as possible to the market.

Capital upgrades are needed at Rooiwal Power Station and complete refurbishment is required at Pretoria West Power Station. However, the City does not have the technical or financial capacity to leverage on the potential of these assets to enhance the City’s energy security, but we do have assets that can be used to secure successful partnerships through a Request for Proposals process.

However, we must first get the public’s inputs into our plans and this is the step that Council approved today.  The public will have 30 days to comment on the proposal, then the matter will return before Council for a final decision.

Reviving the two power stations is important for an energy-secure future for our City. Furthermore, it is important that we manage this process in a transparent and open manner.

title.rendered: Tshwane welcomes agreement to manage water supply challenges

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                         4 September 2023

Cllr Themba Fosi

MMC for Utility Services and Regional Operations and Coordination

Tshwane welcomes agreement to manage water supply challenges

The City of Tshwane is pleased that, following our meeting with the Ministry of  Water and Sanitation, and Rand Water yesterday, all parties have resolved to establish a collaborative framework for addressing water-related issues and to ensure efficient communication channels to better serve residents.

Several key points were deliberated and now pave the way towards the better management of and communication on water supply challenges. These include the following:

  • Proactive monitoring: The City of Tshwane and Rand Water have committed to the proactive continuous monitoring of water levels. When water levels drop to a certain threshold, this information will be promptly shared between the two entities, thus enabling timely interventions to address potential water shortages.
  • Escalation management: A structured decision-making process has been established for dealing with water-related issues that escalate beyond technical matters. When a matter cannot be resolved at technical level, it will be escalated to the responsible MMC. Should it persist, it will be elevated to the Executive Mayor and Rand Water. Should the issue still not be resolved, it will be escalated to the Minister of Water and Sanitation.
  • Water conservation: The City acknowledges the importance of managing our water usage properly and would like to encourage all residents to use water sparingly. We believe that collective action and water-saving efforts by all communities are essential to ensure sustainable water use within Tshwane.

The City of Tshwane remains committed to providing potable water to all our residents. Following weekend supply interruptions, reservoirs in Pretoria East, Soshanguve and Mabopane are showing signs of improvement.

 Enquiries:  MMC  Themba Fosi

(thembamandlaf@tshwane.gov.za)

The City of Tshwane is aware of certain areas within the metropolitan municipality experiencing low water pressure to no water at all as of today, 25 August 2023.

The water shortages are a result of Rand Water’s Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant having suffered a power dip that resulted in the operational failure of the plant, which simply means that it could not pump.

The power dip resulted in the depletion of the following Rand Water systems: 

  • Zwartkopjes System
  • Eikenhof System
  • Mapleton System
  • Palmiet System

Residents are assured that Eskom technicians have since addressed the voltage dip and that all Tshwane reservoir water levels are expected to normalise soon.

During the shutdown, the water utility’s team of technicians was going to repair leaks at Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant as well as replace defective valves at Palmiet Booster Station.

The above-mentioned period of interruption would have had an impact on water provision to the Klipriviersberg, Klipfontein, Brakfontein and Hartebeesthoek Rand Water reservoirs, which supply some of the Tshwane reservoirs.

According to Rand Water, the leaks will be repaired in situ without reducing the load. The other works that require load reduction will be conducted at a later stage when consumption is at reduced levels.

The City apologises for the inconvenience that the above-mentioned cancellation of maintenance work has caused.

title.rendered: Executive Mayor of Tshwane calls on Rand Water to urgently address supply challenges affecting large parts of the city

content.rendered:
Recently, the City of Tshwane has been through a spate of water shortages due to Rand Water failures. The situation has now reached levels that are simply unacceptable. Rand Water is in crisis and this affects us negatively as they are a bulk supplier providing Tshwane with over 70% of its water supply.

This week, the City is yet again experiencing severe water shortages in Soshanguve and Mabopane, leading to some protest action by frustrated residents. In this regard, I would like to call for peace and calm.

We understand the community’s frustrations. The City is fighting to hold Rand Water accountable for its shortcomings, such as no formal communication regarding maintenance schedules.

Currently, Rand Water has embarked on maintenance work at its Hartebeeshoek Reservoir which supplies our Soshanguve L Reservoir. Rand Water indicated that they expect the maintenance work to be completed on Saturday, 22 July 2023.

Furthermore, Rand Water initially assured the City that the water flow to the Soshanguve reservoirs would be supplied via a bypass method but they have failed to deliver.

City teams are reporting no flow into the Soshanguve reservoirs and these reservoirs are effectively running empty. The City has now deployed water tankers as an interim solution while we wait on Rand Water to restore supply.

I have escalated our concerns with Rand Water to the Chairperson of their Board and I have also copied the Minister of Water and Sanitation in the correspondence.

I must also emphasise that these supply challenges are not related to our Rand Water debt, as we are not under any credit control action. We have a payment plan in place which we intend to honour.

We need Rand Water to also play its part, provide us with its telemetry data (reservoir levels), warn us of possible supply interruptions and communicate planned maintenance.

title.rendered: Executive Mayor of Tshwane leads Gauteng government delegation during Rooiwal oversight visit

content.rendered:
This afternoon, I conducted a follow-up oversight visit to Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant with the Gauteng government led by the MEC for Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, Mzi Khumalo, and his Gauteng government colleagues.

The purpose of the visit was to give the provincial government an update on our work to upgrade Rooiwal to ensure a healthy supply of water to Hammanskraal residents.

As previously communicated, we are working with the Department of Water and Sanitation, the National Treasury and the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) to source additional funding to resolve the water challenges in Hammanskraal.

It is estimated that the cost of a full rehabilitation and upgrade of Rooiwal is in the region of R4 billion.

To kick-start the partnership, the City has allocated R450 million towards upgrading Rooiwal over a three-year period.

As part of the project, the DBSA will be appointed as an independent implementing agent. On our part, the City has insisted that no companies implicated in corruption or in the Zondo State Capture Report are awarded any tenders.

We have also taken active measures to blacklist the companies and tenderpreneurs that were awarded the Phase 1 contract to upgrade Rooiwal and failed to do their work. Only 60% of Rooiwal upgrades were completed by the joint venture. We cannot afford another incident of misused public funds at the expense of our residents.

I would like to thank the Gauteng government for their visit and keen interest in working together to fast track  Rooiwal upgrades   and address Hammanskraal water challenges.

title.rendered: Planned upgrade of The Reeds Ext 63 water network

  • Regularly check toilets and taps for leaks.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane and Embassy of Israel join hands on water security

content.rendered:
Earlier today, the City of Tshwane and the Embassy of Israel co-hosted a water security seminar with the aim of sharing the best international practices in water governance.

Water security and stable water supply are very important to us, especially with the ongoing water supply challenges of Rand Water affecting many parts of Tshwane.

Central to our Climate Action Plan, the City of Tshwane has committed itself to providing clean, potable water to all residents and has intentionally partnered with various stakeholders to learn best practices in order to reach this goal.

The state of Israel has excelled in water management and security, and is a world leader in using recycling municipal water. While largely arid, the country has found ways to become completely water sovereign, and this has been the backbone of its extraordinary growth.

Today’s seminar reflected on Israel’s systems to manage water leaks and treat sewage for agricultural use.

The seminar comes at a critical time as the City has recently experienced some water shortages due to Rand Water issues. This means that the City has to start the work   to reduce its reliance on Rand Water, which supplies Tshwane with over 70% of its water.

The City of Tshwane welcomes this collaboration with the Embassy of Israel and other stakeholders to explore new technologies and water governance and conservation systems.

We are open and excited about working with civil rights groups, businesses, non-profit organisations and international partners to learn about the best possible practices on water security, and this seminar is an example of our commitment.

I would like to thank the Embassy of Israel for sharing their expertise with us today.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane Health Department concerned about Rand Water supply challenges impacting clinic operations

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane Health Department notes with concern the recent Rand Water supply challenges affecting the water supply across Tshwane. This is because prolonged water shortages could adversely impact primary healthcare clinic operations.

On 3 July 2023, the City of Tshwane Health Department had to close Olievenhoutbosch Clinic due to water shortages. After the water supply was restored, the clinic reopened on the morning of 4 July 2023. Similarly, Lotus Gardens Clinic has been experiencing a water shortage. Arrangements are currently being made to fill the backup water tank at the facility. The clinic is temporarily open for operations.

As the MMC responsible for Health, I cannot stress more that water shortages have a significant impact on the following:

  • Hygiene practices: Handwashing is not possible after performing clinical procedures as per the infection and control policy.
  • Ablution facilities cannot be flushed.
  • The administration of single dose medication is not possible as patients cannot be offered water to ingest the prescribed treatment.

It is therefore imperative that the water supply be restored to mitigate the possible closure of clinics and to ensure business continuity. Furthermore, cleanliness at our 24 primary healthcare facilities cannot be compromised.

I welcome the City’s technical engagement with Rand Water for intervention so that the water supply can be restored to all affected areas.

The City of Tshwane Health Department will keep communities informed should the situation worsen and force the closure of any of our facilities.

title.rendered: Update at 12:30: Tshwane water supply continues to be affected by power failures impacting on Rand Water infrastructure

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has observed an improvement in most of the reservoirs that were affected over the weekend, such as the Garsfontein and Laudium Reservoirs that had run empty. The said reservoirs have now recovered to 54% and 90%, respectively.

However, some of the areas that remain affected include the Centurion area, as well as new reservoirs, namely the Mooikloof, Klapperkop, Mnandi and Lotus Gardens Reservoirs, which are at critically low levels or empty.

The City wishes to reiterate its clarion call to its customers to drastically reduce water consumption.

Meanwhile, the City’s technical team is engaging with Rand Water for intervention so that the water supply can be restored to all affected areas.

The City of Tshwane has been experiencing challenges of inconsistent water supply following a number of power failures and trips experienced during the month of June at Rand Water’s Vereeniging and Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plants as well as at the Palmiet, Eikenhof and Mapleton Booster Pumping Stations. The utility’s system remains impacted and is struggling to recover.

Reducing water consumption will enable the system to stabilise and recover.

The affected regions are Region 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and parts of 5. Water tankers will be deployed to the areas experiencing water supply challenges.

Residents are reminded and urged to use water wisely and sparingly. Should residents fail to heed this call, the current water outages will be prolonged, resulting in more areas being affected.

The City apologises for the inconvenience that may be encountered.

title.rendered: Tshwane affected by power failures impacting on Rand Water supply infrastructure

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has been notified by Rand Water about inconsistent supply challenges that are underway, affecting Tshwane and other municipalities.

This follows a number of power failures and trips experienced during June 2023 at the Vereeniging and Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plants as well as at the Palmiet, Eikenhof and Mapleton Booster Pumping Stations.

Due to these power failures, the entire water utility system has felt a knock-on effect of unstable supply. This resulted in the depletion of water at the following Rand Water reservoirs:

  • Brakpan
  • Bronberge
  • Hartebeeshoek
  • Klipfontein
  • Selcourt
  • Stompiesfontein
  • Vlakfontein
  • Wildebeesfontein

Rand Water has confirmed that some areas within municipalities are likely to experience low water pressure to no water during the recovery of its system.

This is now evident in the case of the areas north of Pretoria, where there is low water pressure to no water in places like Soshanguve, Mabopane and Ga-Rankuwa.

The Rand Water reservoirs supplying the City of Tshwane are Vlakfontein, Klipfontein, Hartebeeshoek, and Bronberge.

The City encourages residents to assist in conserving water and using water sparingly by adhering to the following:

  • Do not water gardens
  • Do not wash cars
  • Do not clean driveways or pavements using hosepipes
  • Do not fill swimming pools
  • Flush toilets only when necessary
  • Close a running tap while brushing teeth
  • Reduce daily water usage as much as possible

The City of Tshwane apologises for the inconvenience that may be encountered.

In addition, the City appeals to all residents to use water sparingly during this time.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane moves to blacklist companies that failed to complete Rooiwal Phase 1 upgrades

content.rendered:
In the spirit of transparency, clean governance and accountability, I would like to inform our residents that the City has taken active measures to blacklist the companies and tenderpreneurs that were awarded the Phase 1 contract to upgrade Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works.

The joint venture CMS, NJR & Blackhead was appointed in October 2019 in respect of tender USD WS 30-2017/18 for the construction of Phase 1 upgrades and refurbishment of Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works at a cost of R291 996 799,07.

However, the joint venture failed to honour the contract and subjected the Rooiwal Phase 1 upgrades to long delays and continued non-performance, which resulted in the City terminating the contract in August 2022.

After my calls to the City Manager, the City has now resolved to blacklist the joint venture, together with its shareholders and directors, including the state capture accused, Edwin Sodi. The City intends to invoke the provisions of the Preferential Procurement Regulations as stated in Circular 43 of the National Treasury.

Effectively, this means that the joint venture CMS, NJR & Blackhead, as well as its shareholders and directors, will be listed by the National Treasury as restricted suppliers. This will result in these individuals being restricted from doing or obtaining any business with the state for a period of five years.

The Office of the City Manager has written to the affected parties and given them 14 days to respond to our intentions to blacklist them.

The joint venture has only completed 60% of the Rooiwal upgrades despite all the monies spent by the City for Phase 1. Furthermore, a forensic investigation has found that the tender had been awarded irregularly. In this regard, disciplinary steps are currently underway against several City officials who are implicated.

Our multiparty coalition government is determined to fight corruption and to keep our original promise to run a clean, effective and corruption-free administration.

title.rendered: City facilitating social services and relief efforts to assist Hammanskraal residents

content.rendered:
As the MMC responsible for Community and Social Development Services, I recently visited families affected by the cholera outbreak in Hammanskraal to identify their immediate needs and to establish how the City can assist.

As a first step in assisting the grieving families, the City of Tshwane has deployed social workers to offer counselling services.

Additionally, the City distributed packaged personal hygiene essentials, consumable goods and 44 blankets to affected families. This follows the distribution of 10 000 litres of bottled water earlier in the week.

The City will continue to assess the needs of affected families, especially where the main dependent is deceased and children are left without a bread winner, and implement measures required for family support and assistance.

Our multiparty coalition would like to thank all stakeholders who have reached out through various temporary relief donations to minimise the impact of this cholera outbreak.

The City will continue to supply potable water through water tankers while we pursue implementing long-term solutions.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane welcomes donations and relief efforts towards the Hammanskraal community

content.rendered:
I would like to thank Old Mutual and the Red Cross for donating 10 000 litres of bottled water and hygiene packs to Hammanskraal residents today.

Our coalition government welcomes all forms of assistance during this difficult time, and as such I would also like to thank other civic organisations and companies that have assisted our residents, like the Gift of the Givers, Doctors Without Borders, Spar and Coca Cola.

The City is looking at long-terms solutions to address the Hammanskraal water crisis. Last week, the City met with the Department of Water and Sanitation, and we agreed to form a partnership to address this matter urgently and handle the Rooiwal situation on a permanent basis.

We take the delivery of quality water to the residents of Hammanskraal seriously. As such, in our 2023/24 budget the multi-party coalition government allocated R450 million over a period of three years towards the work at Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant.

The City will continue to supply potable water through water tankers while we pursue implementing long-term solutions.

Residents are also reminded to regularly wash the containers they use to draw water from the water tankers with bleach and to boil water drawn from other sources before drinking it.

The City of Tshwane welcomes all efforts that offer temporary relief to the people of Hammanskraal while we pursue implementing long-term solutions.

title.rendered: CITY OF TSHWANE URGES RESIDENTS TO REPORT PEOPLE SELLING UNTESTED WATER IN HAMMANSKRAAL

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has received disturbing news from community members alleging that there are roaming water tankers selling water to residents in Hammanskraal. Communities are cautioned not to buy or drink water from these tankers as it is untested and has not been declared safe for drinking.

The City provides drinkable water to its communities in formal and informal areas in Hammanskraal free of charge. The water provided by the City’s authorised tankers has been declared safe for drinking after a series of tests conducted confirmed that it does not contain cholera.

Officials from the Tshwane Metro Police Department (TMPD) have been activated and will conduct stop-and-search operations on any trucks transporting water without a valid permit. Residents are urged to write down the registration numbers of the tankers selling water and to report these immediately to the TMPD on 012 358 7095/7096. This number is manned 24/7.

Authorities announced the cholera outbreak last weekend in Hammanskraal and surrounding areas after stool test results confirmed that people who presented themselves to health facilities in the area tested positive for cholera. At least 21 people have died of cholera to date.

The City wishes to reiterate its warning to residents not to use tap water for drinking purposes, but rather to use it for washing, cleaning and flushing toilets. The City provides potable (drinkable) water to its communities through its contracted service providers who carry a letter or permit authorising them to dispense water.

Anyone caught selling untested water without a permit will be arrested and prosecuted. Communities are urged to be circumspect of unscrupulous people allegedly taking advantage of the water situation in Hammanskraal by exploiting the vulnerability of people desperate for drinking water.

The City has sampled water for testing from its various water distribution points, including hydrants and reservoirs, and the results have not shown any trace of cholera. Confirmatory test results from the National Institute for Communicable Diseases that will pinpoint the actual source of contamination are still outstanding.

title.rendered: Human Settlements Department ramps up water provision through water tankers to Hammanskraal after cholera outbreak

content.rendered:
Following the outbreak of cholera in the Hammanskraal area, I have instructed the Human Settlements Department to increase the provision of water tankers from three days to five days a week in the affected areas until 31 May 2023.

The City will then assess the need to continue with the increased days. The allotted days for the provision of water tankers are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday. The following areas are affected:

  • Bridgeview
  • Chris Hani Block G (Erf 3742 and 10442, Kudube Unit 10)
  • Hammanskraal Ext 2 (Erf 3503)
  • Hammanskraal West Ext 10
  • Hammanskraal West Ext 4 (Portion 9 and 10 and Sekampaneng)
  • Kudube Unit 9 (Hammanskraal Portion 9)
  • Nkandla (Stinkwater area)
  • Phomolong (Suurman Ridge)
  • Prestige
  • Soutpan/Marikana (New Eersterus Ext 8, 9, 10 and 11), Hammanskraal
  • Steve Biko

The city would like to encourage residents in the affected areas to regularly wash the containers they use to draw water from the water tankers with bleach detergent, and to boil water drawn from other sources before drinking it.

It is important to note that City testing results from multiple sites around Temba and Hammanskraal have come back negative for E. Coli and cholera.

However, the City is still awaiting the confirmatory test results from the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) to determine the actual source of contamination.

I would like to send out my heartfelt condolences to the families of the residents who have succumbed to the illness and wish a speedy recovery to those hospitalised.

title.rendered: UPDATE: CITY TESTING ON MULTIPLE SITES INDICATE ZERO CHOLERA DETECTED FROM PIPED WATER SUPPLY

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has received the results from sampling testing taken from multiple sites around Temba and Hammanskraal pertaining to tracing the cholera outbreak.

Multiple reservoirs, fire hydrants, primary schools, clinics and other locations that receive water from Temba Water Treatment Plant were tested. All of these tests have conclusively indicated that there are no microbiological contaminants that point to E. Coli or faecal coliforms that can be linked to the cholera outbreak.

This means that the water that is being distributed via the City’s bulk water distribution network in the area does not have cholera present in it. This does not make this water safe to drink as it is heavily treated with chlorine. Various points where water tankers draw their supply have also been tested.

The City has widened the scope of its testing and has been interviewing various patients to assist in tracing the source of the contamination. We will continue to keep affected residents updated on further test results as and when they become available.

It is critically important that residents who have symptoms present themselves early at their nearest clinic or hospital in order to be treated. Please do not wait until you feel worse. We urge all residents in the area to take extra precaution with good hygiene practices.

Below is a list of sites where samples were tested and results came out negative for cholera from 18 to 21 May 2023:

  • Adam Masebe Secondary School
  • Babelegi Reservoir Klipdrift
  • Eersterus Hydrant
  • House 143 Stellenbosch Temba
  • Hydrant from Magalies
  • Jana Laubscher, Brenner Mills, Hammanskraal West Reservoir
  • Jubilee Hospital Tower
  • Kanana Ward 49 Car Wash
  • Kanana Ward 49 Zion CC
  • KLT Automative 10th Street Admin Kitchen
  • Mandela Mokonyama Primary School
  • Renstown Reservoir, Temba
  • Suurman Clinic
  • Tanker Truck (registration plate known)
  • Temba NW, Jubilee Hospital Tower
  • Temba NW, Leboneng Primary School
  • Temba NW, Manyathi High School
  • Temba NW, SAPS College
  • Temba Oustad B, Demploy Training Centre

The City will intensify its food safety campaign, which includes, but is not limited to, how to hygienically prepare, transport and store food in the Hammanskraal area.

While the water supplied by the City in Hammanskraal is not potable, the City has been providing potable water through 52 water tankers to informal settlements three times a week. The number of days has been increased to five times a week following the cholera outbreak, except on Thursdays and Sundays, until the end of May 2023.

In addition, the City provides 44 water trucks daily to formal areas in Region 2. All this is done to ensure that communities have safe drinking water.

Cholera is a bacterial disease usually spread through contaminated water. It causes severe diarrhoea and dehydration. If left untreated, it can be fatal in a matter of hours, even in previously healthy people.

The City of Tshwane would like to reiterate its appeal to the communities in Hammanskraal and surrounding areas to refrain from using water from taps for drinking purposes.

Outbreak response teams are on the ground conducting surveillance monitoring, sampling and field investigations. The City is eagerly awaiting the confirmatory test results from the National Institute for Communicable Diseases to determine the actual source of contamination.

The City would like to encourage residents in the affected areas to regularly wash the containers they use to draw water from the water tankers with bleach and to boil water drawn from other sources before drinking it. Communities are also urged not to conduct religious activities, such as baptisms, in rivers or streams.

title.rendered: BATHO BA BA NNANG KWA HAMMANSKRAAL LE DIKAROLO TSE DI MO TIKOLOGONG YA YONE BA KOPIWA GORE BA SE KA BA NWA METSI A A TSWANG MO DIPOMPONG KA NTLHA YA LEWO LA BOLWETSE

content.rendered:
Toropokgolo ya Tshwane e rata go baagi ba kwa Hammanskraal le mafelo a a maapi go se dirise nwe metsi a a tswang mo dipompong  ka ntlha ya lewo le le tlisitseng bolwetse mo lefelong leo.

Le fa gone metsi a a tlamelwang ke Toropokgolo kwa Hammanskraal, e se a a nowang, Toropokgolo eno e romela metsi a a nowang ka ditanka tsa metsi di le 52 go ya kwa mafelong a baipei ka makgetlo a le mararo mo bekeng, le  go romela dilori tsa metsi di le 40 ka tsatsi  go ya kwa mafelong a a kwadisitsweng a a kwa Kgaolong ya 2. Seno se dirwa go netefatsa fa batho ba nwa metsi a a phepa.

Toropokgolo e dira diteko ka metlha tsa boleng jwa metsi a a abelwang baagi ba rona. Mme morago ga go runya ga lewo leno, go tla dirwa diteko tse di tseneletseng mo netewekeng yotlhe ya metsi.

Go tserwe disampole tsa metsi mo mafelong a a amilweng ke bolwetse jono mme a rometswe gore go dirwe diteko go tlhomamisa gore ke eng se se bakileng bolwetse jono ,mme go dipoelo tsa diteko di solofetswe ka Laboraro. Bangwe ba batho ba ba tshwerweng ke bolwetse jono, ba kwa kgaolong ya Moretele e e sa tlamelweng ke Toropokgolo ya Tshwane.

Gompieno badiredi ba Lefapha la Boitekanelo la Toropokgolo ba tla boela gape kwa mafelong a a amegileng go tsaya disampole tse dingwe go tswa mo ditankeng tsa metsi tse di tlamelang metse ya baipei ka metsi.

Ditlhopha tsa tsibogelo ya go runya ga lewo  di mo lefelong leo go dira tiro ya go tlhokomela le go tsaya disampole tsa metsi. Batho ba rotloediwa go ya kwa lefelong la kalafi le le gaufi ka bonako fela fa ba itemogela matshwao a bolwetse. Ditheo tsa boitekanelo di nna di eme sejaro go thusa ka bonako balwetse ba ba nang le matshwao a bolwetse.

Toropokgolo e emetse dipoelo ka tlhoafalo, tse di tswang go Setheo sa Bosetšhaba sa Malwetse a a Fetelang (NICD) go tlhomamisa se se bakileng lewo leno.

Toropokgolo eno e rata go rotloetsa baagi ba mafelo a a amilweng ke lewo leno gore ka metlha ba tlhatswe dikgamelo tse ba di dirisang go gelela metsi a a tswang mo ditankeng ka Jik, le go bedisa metsi a a tswang mo metsweding e mengwe pele ba a nwa. Mme e bile batho ba rotloediwa go se dire ditiro tsa bodumedi tse di jaaka go kolobetsa mo dinokeng kgotsa mo melatswaneng.

title.rendered: VHADZULAPO VHA HA HAMMANSKRAAL NA VHUPO HA NGA TSINI VHA KHOU ELETSHEDZWA URI VHA SONGO NWA MAḒI A BOMMBI NGA MURAHU HA U TSHIWO TSHA DZWADZE

content.rendered:
Ḓorobo khulwane ya Tshwane i khou tama u eletshedza vhadzulapo vha ha Hammanskraal na vha vhupo ha tsini uri vha songo nwa maḓi a bommbini nga murahu ha tshiwo tsha dwadze kha vhupo honoho.

Nga mulandu wa uri maḓi ane a khou ṋetshedzwa nga Ḓorobo khulwane kha vhupo ha Hammanskraal ha ngo tea u nwiwa, Ḓorobo khulwane i khou ṋetshedza maḓi o teaho u nwiwa nga u shumisa mathannga maḓi a swikaho 52 kha vhupo ha vhudzulo ha mikhukhuni luraru nga vhege khathihi na maṱhiraka a u hwala maḓi a swikaho 40 kha vhupo ha vhudzulo ho dzudzanyeaho ḓuvha ḽiṅwe na ḽiṅwe kha Dzingu ḽa 2. Hezwi zwi khou itelwa uri vhadzulapo vha kone u wana maḓi a u nwa o kunaho.

Ḓorobo khulwane i dzulela u ita ndingo dza nga ha vhuḓi ha maḓi ane a ṋetshedzwa vhadzulapo vhashu. Nga murahu ha tshiwo itshi tsha dwadze, hu khou ḓo itwa ndingo dzo fhelelaho kha netiweke yoṱhe ya nḓisedzo ya maḓi nga u angaredza.

Ho kuvhanganywa sambula dza maḓi u bva kha vhupo ho kwameaho u itela uri dzi kone u lingwa nahone hu khou lavhelelwa uri mvelelo dza hone, sa izwi dzi dzone dzine dza ḓo ṱalusa tshivhangi tsha tshiwo tsha dwadze iḽi, dzi ḓo wanala nga Ḽavhuraru. Zwiṅwe zwa zwiwo zwe zwa vhigwa, ndi zwine zwa bva kha vhupo ha Moretele, vhune ha vha vhupo vhune ha si ṋetshedzwe maḓi nga Masipala wa Ḓorobo khulwane ya Tshwane.

Vhaofisiri vha bvaho kha Muhasho wa Mutakalo wa Ḓorobo khulwane vha ḓo dovha hafhu vha dalela vhupo ho kwameaho ṋamusi u itela u kuvhanganya dziṅwe sambula hafhu u bva kha mathannga a maḓi ane a ṋetshedza maḓi kha vhupo ha vhudzulo ha mikhukhuni.

Zwigwada zwa u lwa na zwiwo zwa dwadze, na zwone zwi kati, zwi khou ita mushumo wa vhulavhelesi khathihi na u ita ndingo kha maḓi ayo. Vhadzulapo vha khou eletshedzwa uri vha ḓivhonadze henefho kha tshiimiswa tsha zwa mutakalo tshi re tsini navho nga u ṱavhanya arali vha tshi khou ḓiwana vhe na tsumbadwadze. Zwiimiswa zwa mutakalo zwi khou dzula zwo ḓilugisela u ṱhaṱhuvha vhalwadze vhoṱhe vhane vha vha na tsumbadwadze nga u ṱavhanya.

Ḓorobo khulwane i khou dzula yo lindela mvelelo dza ndingo idzi u itela uri i ḓo kona u khwaṱhisedza tshivhangi tsha tshiwo tsha dwadze iḽi u bva kha vha Tshiimiswa tsha Malwadze a Phirela tsha Lushaka.

Ḓorobo khulwane i khou tama u ṱuṱuwedza vhadzulapo vha vhupo ho kwameaho uri vha dzule vha tshi ṱanzwa zwigubu zwavho nga bleach misi yoṱhe hu tshi katelwa na zwiṅwe zwoṱhe zwine vha zwi shumisa u ka ngazwo maḓi u bva kha mathannga ayo a maḓi khathihi na u vhilisa maḓi ayo e vha a ka u bva kha zwiṅwe zwiko zwa maḓi phanḓa ha musi vha tshi nga a nwa. Vhadzulapo vha khou dovha hafhu vha eletshedzwa uri vha songo ita mishumo ya zwa vhurereli u fana na ndovhedzo, ngomu milamboni kana kha milambwana.

title.rendered: BADUDI BA HAMMANSKRAAL LE BA MAFELOMABAPI BA KGOPELWA GORE BA SE NWE MEETSE A GO TŠWA DIPOMPONG MORAGO GA GO PHULEGA GA BOLWETŠI

content.rendered:
Toropokgolo ya Tshwane e tšea sebaka se go kgopela badudi ka moka ba Hammanskraal le ba mafelomabapi gore ba se nwe meetse a go tšwa dipompong morago ga gore go phulege bolwetši tikologong yeo.

Le ge e le gore meetse ao Toropokgolo e ya abelago tikologo ya Hammanskraal a se a go nwewa, Toropokgolo e abela mafelo a mekhukhung ka meetse a go nwewa ka ditanka tša meetse tše 52 makga a mararo ka beke, gotee le dilori tša meetse tša go lekana 40 makheišeneng a Selete sa 2 tšatši ka tšatši. Se se direlwa go netefatša gore badudi ba nale meetse a go nwa a go bolokega.

Toropokolo nako le nako e dula e dira diteko tša khwalithi ya meetse ao a abelwago badudi ba rena, ka gona, morago ga bolwetši bjo, diteko tše di tseneletšego di tlo dirwa mo matamong le diphaepheng ka moka tša go sepediša meetse.

Go tšeerwe disampolo tša meetse mafelong ao a amegilego le go išwa ditekong ebile dipoelo tša ona di letetšwe ka Laboraro go bona gore sebakwa sa bolwetši bjo ke sefe. Tše dingwe tša diphetelo tše di begilwego di tšwa tikologong ya Moretele, yeo e sa abelwego meetse ke Toropokgolo ya Tshwane.

Bašomedi go tšwa Kgorong ya Maphelo ya Toropokgolo ba tla goroga gapegape lehono mafelong ao a amegilego go tšea disampolo tše dingwe go tšwa ditankeng tša meetse tše di abelago mafelo a mekhukhung ka meetse.

Sehlophatšhomo sa go šetšana le go phulega ga malwetši se gona mafelong ao go bea seemo leihlo le go dira disampolo tša meetse. Badudi ba kgopelwa go leba maokelong a kgauswi ge ba bona goba ba itemogela dika tša bolwetši bjo. Maokelo le ona a ntšhitše mahlo dinameng go hlaganela ka tšhoganyetšo balwetši ba go laetša dika tša bolwetši bjo.

Toropokgolo e sa letetše dipoelo tša kgonthišišo ya diteko go tšwa go Setheo sa Bosetšhaba sa Malwetši a go Fetelana (NICD) go hwetša sebakwa sa bolwetši bjo.

Toropokgolo e rata go hlohleletša badudi ka moka go tšwa mafelong ao a amegilego go hlatswa ka bleach dikhontheina tša bona tše ba di dirišago go kga meetse go tšwa ditankeng tše kgolo, le go bidiša meetse ao a tšwago methopong ye mengwe pele ba ka a nwa. Badudi ba kgopelwa gape gore ba se phethagatše ditiragalo tša sedumedi go swana le dikolobetšo ka dinokeng goba ka gare ga meela ya meetse.

title.rendered: VAAKI VA LE HAMMANSKRAAL NA TINDHAWU TA LE KUSUHI VA KHUTAZIWA LESWAKU VA NGA NWI MATI YO HUMA ESWIPHAYIPHANINI ENDZHAKU KA NTUNGU

content.rendered:
Dorobankulu ra Tshwane ri rhandza ku khutaza vaaki va le Hammanskraal na tindhawu ta le kusuhi leswaku va nga nwi mati yo huma eswiphayiphanini endzhaku ka ntungu eka ndhawu ya vona.

Leswi mati lawa ya phakeriwaka hi Dorobankulu eHammanskraal ya nga ringanelangiki ku nwiwa, Dorobankulu ri phakela mati lawa ya nwekaka hi ku tirhisa 52 wa tilori ta mati ku ya eka tindzhawu leti nga riki ta ximfumo ka nharhu hi vhiki, na 40 wa tilori ta mati kuya eka tindhawu ta ximfumo siku na siku eka Rhijini 2. Leswi swi endleriwa ku tiyisisa leswaku vaaki na mati yo nwa lama hlayisekeke.

Dorobankulu ri tshama ri ri karhi ri endla swikambelo swa nkoka wa mati lama nyikiwaka vaaki va hina.  Endzhaku ka ntungu lowu, ku ta endliwa swikambelo leswi heleleke eka netiweke hinkwayo ya ku phakeriwa ka mati.

Tisampulu ta mati ti tekiwile eka tindhawu leti khumbekeke naswona ti ta ya kamberiwa, mbuyelo wu languteriwile hi Ravunharhu ku kumisisa xivangelo xa ntungu. Tin’wana ta timhangu leti vikiweke ti huma eka ndhawu ya Moretele, leyi nga phakeriwiki hi Dorobankulu ra Tshwane.

Vatirhi kusuka eka Ndzawulo ya Rihanyo ya Dorobankulu va ta ya eka tindhawu leti khumbekeke nakambe namuntlha ku ya hlengeleta tisampulu tin’wana kusuka eka tilori ta mati leti phakelaka mati eka tindhawu to ka ti nga ri ta ximfumo.

Swipanu swa nhlamulo wa ntungu swi le ku tirheni ntirho wo landzelerisa na ku teka tisampulu ta mati.  Vaaki va khutaziwa ku ya eka ndhawu ya swa rihanyo ya le kusuhi hi xihatla loko va va na swikombiso swa vuvabyi. Switirhisiwa swa swa rihanyo swi tshama swi vambile ngoma leswaku swi ta kota ku tshungula vavabyi lava nga na swikombiso hi xihatla.

Dorobankulu ri rindzele hi mahlongati mbuyelo wa swikambelo swo tiyisisa kusuka eka Nhlangano wa Rixaka wa Mavabyi yo Tlulela ku kumisisa xivangelo xa ntungu.

Dorobankulu ri khutaza vaaki va tindhawu leti khumbekaka ku tshamela ku hlantswa swibye leswi va swi tirhisaka ku ka mati kusuka tilori ta mati hi xibasisi xa bleach, na ku virisa mati lama va ma keke kusuka eka swihlovo swin’wana loko va nga si ma nwa. Vaaki va tlhela va khutaziwa ku ka va nga endli mitirho ya swa vukhongeri yo fana na ku khuvula emilambyeni.

title.rendered: CITY OF TSHWANE TO DO SAMPLE TESTS ON WATER DRAWN FROM FIRE HYDRANTS AND INSPECT THE CLEANLINESS OF WATER TANKERS

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane’s team of Environmental Health Practitioners has resolved to run tests on water drawn from all fire hydrants and inspect the cleanliness of water tankers providing water to the communities in the Hammanskraal supply area. This process will run for the whole week.

This comes in the wake of the cholera outbreak declared by the Gauteng MEC for Health yesterday.

Initially, the sampling of water was going to be confined to the Rooiwal hydrant only, but a decision was taken to expand sampling to all the hydrants and water tankers supplying water to the informal and formal areas in and around Hammanskraal. Tests will also be done on the Temba Waste Water Treatment Plant.

The average period to get the test results of sampled water from laboratories is three days.

The City will intensify its food safety campaign, which includes, but is not limited to, how to hygienically prepare, transport and store food in the Hammanskraal area.

Yesterday, the Gauteng Department of Health announced an outbreak of cholera in Hammanskraal and surrounding areas after the release of positive cholera test results for stool samples that were collected from 19 patients who had presented at the Jubilee District Hospital.

To date, 12 people have been confirmed dead, 99 are being managed at the emergency unit and 37 have been admitted to wards.

The City of Tshwane is working closely with the Gauteng Department of Health to limit the mortality rate and to reduce the spread of the disease.

title.rendered: COMMUNITIES IN HAMMANSKRAAL AND SURROUNDING AREAS URGED NOT TO DRINK WATER FROM TAPS FOLLOWING AN OUTBREAK

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane would like to urge communities in Hammanskraal and surrounding areas not to use water from taps for drinking purposes following an outbreak in the area.

While the water supplied by the City in Hammanskraal is not potable, the City provides drinkable water through 52 water tankers to informal settlements three times a week and 40 water trucks to formal areas daily in Region 2. This is done to ensure that communities have safe drinking water.

The City regularly conducts tests on the quality of water provided to our communities. Following this outbreak, comprehensive tests will be done on the entire water distribution network.

Water samples have been collected in the affected areas and taken for tests, and results are expected on Wednesday to determine the cause of the outbreak. Some of the cases reported are from the Moretele area, which is not supplied by the City of Tshwane.

Officials from the City’s Health Department will go to the affected areas again today to collect further samples from the water tankers that supply water to the informal settlements.

Outbreak response teams are on the ground conducting surveillance monitoring and sampling the water. Communities are urged to present themselves to their nearest health facility immediately when they experience symptoms. Health facilities are on high alert to urgently attend to patients with symptoms.

The City is eagerly awaiting the confirmatory test results from the National Institute for Communicable Diseases to establish the cause of the outbreak.

The City would like to encourage residents in the affected areas to regularly wash the containers they use to draw water from the water tankers with bleach and to boil water drawn from other sources before drinking it. Communities are also urged not to conduct religious activities, such as baptisms, in rivers or streams.

title.rendered: Urgent repair of Laudium Reservoir main feeder pipe

content.rendered:
Yesterday afternoon, 9 May 2023, the outgoing pipe of Laudium Reservoir was badly damaged by the contractor responsible for upgrading work at the reservoir. Unfortunately, the operational team cannot isolate the pipe at the reservoir because of technical challenges. This means that the reservoir needs to drain completely before we can begin repairing the reservoir.

Our operational team was on-site this morning at 06:00 to confirm whether the reservoir had drained so that work could start, but there is still some water flowing out. Our current estimate is that repairs should start at around 09:00. The estimated duration of the repair is three hours from when we start, although we can only confirm that once repairs begin.

After the repair is complete, there will be an additional delay in restoring water as we need to refill the reservoir. Laudium Reservoir is a high-lying reservoir and we need to build sufficient pressure in the reservoir to ensure that all residents get water.

Based on this timeline, residents should plan for the water supply to be interrupted for most of the day today.

Residents in Laudium, Claudius and Christoburg will be affected by this water interruption.

We will communicate more information via councillors and the City’s communication team as we reach repair milestones.

title.rendered: Executive Mayor of Tshwane conducts oversight visit to Mamelodi to assess basic service delivery

content.rendered:
Earlier today, I conducted a service delivery oversight visit to various parts of Mamelodi, including the very busy Tsamaya Avenue, Nelson Mandela Park and Solomon Mahlangu Square.

During the oversight visit I was joined by MMC Grandi Theunissen, City officials and local councillors. We all walked around certain areas to monitor and assess service delivery levels to communities.

I was pleased to note maintenance work taking place, such as repairing high-mast lights, cutting grass and building speed humps in Tsamaya Avenue. While this is good basic service delivery, the reality is that there are many challenges in Mamelodi that need to be addressed, including the state of the electricity and water infrastructure in the area.

The visit to Mamelodi follows my oversight visit to Soshanguve in Region 1 on Friday and other parts of Pretoria North where we visited various substations to get a clear picture of the state of our critical infrastructure.

I want to remind residents that I have set the following five core priorities that will ensure that we fast-track service delivery for all:

  1. Stabilise City finances by devising and implementing a bold recovery plan that focuses on the core functions of the municipality.
  2. Reduce the number of unscheduled water and electricity outages, invest in our core infrastructure and mitigate the effects of load-shedding (reduce reliance on Eskom).
  3. Improve basic services pertaining to pothole repairs, street light maintenance, grass cutting and public cleaning.
  4. Secure infrastructure assets, main roads and business nodes against criminals by improving the focus and functioning of the Tshwane Metro Police Department.
  5. Instil high levels of productivity and professionalism in City officials through appropriate performance management systems.

Conducting service delivery oversight visits forms a key part of our work. It is important that we have our eyes and ears on the ground to better respond to the needs of our residents.

title.rendered: Eskom load-shedding has a damaging impact on our electricity infrastructure and this can lead to prolonged power outages

content.rendered:
Eskom has again announced that it would raise load-shedding to Stage 6 this week until further notice. Raised levels of load-shedding are a crisis for our municipality, affecting both the condition of our electricity network as well as our ability to attend to outages.

Stage 6 load-shedding means that rolling blackouts will affect regions of Tshwane two to three times a day for a total time without electricity at a minimum of six hours per day. Our networks were never designed for load-shedding and continuously turning the electricity network off and on has a major impact on the condition of our network infrastructure.

Residents are already aware that load-shedding can result in additional outages due to overloading the network, as well as vandalism and theft of the City of Tshwane’s infrastructure. However, as the frequency of load-shedding increases, City resources will be stretched with just switching areas off and on. The same teams needed to perform this switching also play a critical role in electricity network repair and maintenance work, and will have significantly less time available to work on restoring electricity on outages that are not related to load-shedding.

The electricity teams of the Energy and Electricity Department and the Regional Operations and Coordination Department are working determinedly to face this immense pressure on our electricity network, but the reality is that our system is not designed to cope with this situation. The heavy rains we have been experiencing recently are also making this situation worse, with wet weather increasing the likelihood of equipment faults. This situation is very serious for the entire Tshwane.

I must again request residents to be active in playing a role in helping the City manage this difficult time. Please turn off your appliances during load-shedding, leaving only a light on to let you know when the power returns, and then only turn your appliances back on after some time has passed (10 to 20 minutes). The surges generated as power is turned back on cause areas to trip minutes after having been restored, causing extended outages in some areas. Ensure that energy-intensive appliances are off during peak times (particularly from 18:00 to 21:00), such as your geyser, to assist in decreasing the load and preventing a bad situation from worsening.

We continue to pursue long-term interventions to see what the City can do to alleviate this continuous challenge. This includes launching our Energy Task Team, who are looking at alternative electricity solutions, including renewable energy and power from independent power producers.

In the interim, we all need to work together to best manage this difficult time.

title.rendered: Electricity outage affects Rand Water’s Mapleton Booster Pump Station

content.rendered:
On Sunday, 7 May 2023, Rand Water experienced multiple power failures at the Mapleton Booster Pumping Station, which is the water pumping station that supplies Pretoria East and various surrounding areas. The City has been in communication with Rand Water since the start of this outage. The first outage was resolved relatively quickly and while seemly maintaining partial flow, we received notice late last night that the power had gone off again, which resulted in a total stoppage in pumping water. The communication we received this morning is that the electricity supply has been restored to Mapleton this morning at 02:24, and it has been pumping at full load since then.

This incident has resulted in many Rand Water reservoirs, specifically Rand Water’s Bronberg and Vlakfontein 1 and 2 Reservoirs, dropping to critically low levels. Rand Water has urged all customers to use water sparingly as some areas within Tshwane are likely to experience low water pressure to no water pressure while the reservoirs refill.

We will monitor the situation and do what we can to mitigate potential shortages.

In the meanwhile, the Executive Mayor has requested information from Rand Water regarding the water tightness test they planned to start on Friday that would continue for a period of five days (from 12 to 17 May 2023). We had been pushing to fill our reservoirs ahead of this operation in order to limit any effect it may have on our water supply, however, this outage will negatively affect such preparation efforts.

Our Communication, Marketing and Events Department will provide additional detail on this outage during the day, and we will communicate further should we get reports of further outages or challenges.

Please continue to limit your water usage, so that we can work to fill our reservoirs to ensure that they are as full as we can get them on 12 May 2023.

We apologise for this inconvenience and will keep working to resolve the ongoing water challenges in Pretoria East and surrounds.

title.rendered: City working to restore final areas in Pretoria East affected by the water outage and on the way forward

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has been working with the final communities affected by the water outage in Pretoria East throughout the weekend. I have been out on-site at reservoirs and pump stations with officials and affected community members.

As of this morning, I can confirm that almost all areas have water restored and our reservoirs have sufficient supply to maintain provision to most areas. However, we are aware of a few remaining estates that continue to experience water challenges and we are working with management and ward councillors to resolve these.

This extended outage was unprecedented as we have never had a situation where the supply from Rand Water was completely shut down for over three days. Previously, we have had partial supply issues or the supply outages had been shorter.

While we continue to work with Mooikloof Estate, Tygervalley Country Estate and Leeuwenhof Estate to restore water to these final areas, we are also focusing on taking actions to prepare for and hopefully mitigate or prevent future outages.

We are looking at the functioning of various pump stations in areas like Mooikloof and Carina to boost the resilience of our system. Where a fix is needed, we are prioritising that. Where an upgrade is needed, we are looking at securing the budget to enable such. Within our system we are looking at areas we can strengthen to maximise our ability to use the existing supply we have.

The reality is that the majority of Tshwane’s water is supplied by Rand Water, and we are looking to strengthen our relationship and communication with them. We need an open and transparent line of active communication so that we can best respond to any future challenges.

To this effect, I already met with Mr David Mahlobo, Deputy Minister of Water and Sanitation, last week Friday on-site at Rand Water’s reservoirs to sensitise the national government about this situation. I must thank the Deputy Minister for coming on short notice and for his proactive stance on this issue.

title.rendered: MMC for Health welcomes the opening of a new municipal health services office in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
As the MMC responsible for Health in the City of Tshwane, I am pleased to announce that the City of Tshwane Health Department opened a new municipal health services (MHS) office at 113 Lovers Lane, Mandela Village, Hammanskraal (Tshwane Metro Police Department offices). The office opened on 4 April 2023.

The purpose of the new MHS office is to bring service delivery and accessibility closer to the community and reduce travelling costs to other MHS offices.

Our MHS offices provide  important services which include  the following:

  • Compliance monitoring of water quality, including water sampling and testing, and mapping of water sources in relation to pollution and contamination
  • Environmental health promotion and hygiene awareness
  • Monitoring food safety and hygiene
  • Monitoring waste management and disposal, and control of communicable diseases
  • Monitoring environmental pollution, including air and noise pollution

By accessing the Mandela Village office, community members can register MHS-related complaints and receive assistance with certificates of acceptability for food premises, health certificates for early childhood development centres (crèches) and certificates of competence for funeral undertakers. The City therefore hopes to improve turnaround times in relation to MHS complaints and certification.

Overall, MHS is an important function and aims to reduce diseases and ensure a clean, healthy and safe environment for the communities of Tshwane. I would like to encourage community members to make use of these services.

title.rendered: Pretoria East reservoirs witnessing significant recovery, City efforts will now move to assist high-lying areas

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has seen improvement across most of the areas affected by the water outage in Pretoria East. Our focus will now move to interventions focused on restoring water to high-lying areas, while also maintaining the stability of the areas that have already been restored.

Reservoirs, like Parkmore LL Reservoir at 86%, Waverley LL Reservoir at 99% and Monumentpark Reservoir at 67%, show significant recovery. Eersterust and Mamelodi have restored supply, although high water usage is still a concern, preventing significant capacity building up in their respective reservoirs, but water is flowing to those communities.

The main intervention today, now that our Garsfontein Reservoir has recovered to a healthy level of 73%, is to begin throttling the supply from Garsfontein to allow us to channel water to Grootfontein and Mooikloof. This process will take some time but should result in faster restoration to these high-lying and further-away reservoirs. We will also manage the process to prevent compromising any of the areas dependent on Garsfontein.

Due to this intervention to restore water to areas without water, some of the areas with restored water may experience low water pressure. This should not be a cause for concern as we will carefully monitor and manage the situation to do our best to prevent water from running out again.

We are all in this together and we need to help our community as a whole. That is why I again ask that residents who have had their water restored must please continue to take reasonable caution to limit their water usage. For the next couple of days, please take showers and not baths. Please do not wash your cars or water your garden. These types of personal actions will all assist in speeding up water supply to residents who have not received any water yet.

Water tankers are still being deployed to affected areas, and we will not stand down this service until we have confirmed that all areas are fully restored. Thank you for working with us, and I will communicate again this evening to report on progress.
